item.title: Dodgers Reportedly Among Teams Showing Interest In 2.42 ERA Free Agent Pitcher
item.description: Relief pitcher Jonathan Loaisiga The Los Angeles Dodgers could be targeting relievers this offseason, and according to MLB Network's Jon Morosi , they are among the teams interested in Jonathan Loáisiga. Loáisiga spent the first eight years of his career with the New York Yankees. He had a solid tenure, posting a 3.54 ERA in 193 games. However, he had a 4.25 ERA in 2025. He signed a one-year deal with the Arizona Diamondbacks and had a great bounce-back year. He had a 2.42 ERA in 67 games for the Snakes. He did a great job keeping the ball in the ballpark, giving up just three home runs after allowing seven homers in 2025 for the Yankees. Loáisiga would be a great addition to the Dodgers' bullpen, especially if they lose Blake Treinen, Alex Vesia and Kris Bubic. Bubic was a starter for the Kansas City Royals but was used out of the bullpen in Los Angeles. Loáisiga is a right-hander, so he could be a good replacement for Treinen. Loáisiga ranked in the 96th percentile for walk rate, 93rd percentile for chase rate, 95th percentile for ground ball rate and 92nd percentile for hard-hit rate. According to Morosi, there are five teams involved in his market right now. The Dodgers may have to beat out other suitors, but they can provide Loáisiga a chance to compete for a championship on a roster with plenty of superstars. Other teams may not be able to do the same. More MLB: Red Sox Reportedly Considering Cutting Ties With $60 Million Outfielder

item.title: Ireland shake off sluggish start to brush aside Fiji
item.description: Nations Championship Ireland (17) 43 Tries: O'Brien 2, Baloucoune 2, Kelleher, Porter, Timoney Cons: Prendergast 3, Frawley Fiji (15) 15 Tries: Tuisova, Yato Con: Volavola Pen: Volavola Ireland recovered from a sluggish first-half performance to wear down spirited Fiji and keep alive their hopes of topping the Nations Championship northern hemisphere table with a bonus-point win in Dublin. After thumping Argentina last week, Ireland failed to click in an unconvincing opening, with Tommy O'Brien's early try and a Robert Baloucoune double enough for a 17-15 lead. Fiji arrived in Dublin without a win in nine previous meetings against their hosts, and having been thrashed 54-17 by France last week. But they dreamed of a historic win after tries from Josua Tuisova and Peceli Yato, and a Ben Volavola penalty, kept them firmly in the contest at the break. However, Ronan Kelleher, Andrew Porter and O'Brien crossed as Andy Farrell's men scored 26 unanswered second-half points to deny the Pacific Islanders, who remain without a point in the competition. The result left Ireland one point off northern hemisphere leaders France - and behind England on points difference - before next week's mouthwatering tussle with world champions South Africa in Dublin as they look to seal a spot in the inaugural competition's Twickenham showpiece on 29 November. Nations Championship: Ireland fight back to earn bonus-point win over Fiji - reaction Fiji frustrate slow-starting Irish When these sides last met, in Dublin two years ago, Ireland scored four converted tries to effectively end the contest by half-time on their way to a 52-17 win. But this was anything but simple. Despite making seven changes from last week's victory over the Pumas and losing centre Jamie Osborne to an early injury, Ireland threatened to gallop into the distance in a hurry. The back three of Hansen, Baloucoune and O'Brien connected to put the latter in for an eighth-minute try - the wing atoning for an earlier knock-on. Gibson-Park, back in the starting line-up, thought he had added a second for Ireland, but the scrum-half lost control of the ball as he touched down. From there, Fiji decided to get moving and hit back quickly when mountainous centre Tuisova barged over the line after a piercing carry by Yato. Yato, who took over the captaincy from Tevita Ikanivere for Saturday's game, then touched down himself after winger Juta Wainiqolo surged through a hole in the home defence. Irish frustration deepened when Ryan Baird was stopped just short of the line but, after a superb Prendergast kick caused havoc in the Fijian defence, the fly-half put Baloucoune in after good work from the impressive Hansen. Fiji, playing with rising confidence, responded when prop Luke Tagi burst over, but Isoa Nasilasila was adjudged to have knocked the ball in the away side's line-out. After thumping Argentina last week, Ireland failed to click in an unconvincing opening, with Tommy O'Brien's early try and a Robert Baloucoune double enough for a 17-15 lead. Fiji arrived in Dublin without a win in nine previous meetings against their hosts, and having been thrashed 54-17 by France last week. But they dreamed of a historic win after tries from Josua Tuisova and Peceli Yato, and a Ben Volavola penalty, kept them firmly in the contest at the break. However, Ronan Kelleher, Andrew Porter and O'Brien crossed as Andy Farrell's men scored 26 unanswered second-half points to deny the Pacific Islanders, who remain without a point in the competition. The result left Ireland one point off northern hemisphere leaders France - and behind England on points difference - before next week's mouthwatering tussle with world champions South Africa in Dublin as they look to seal a spot in the inaugural competition's Twickenham showpiece on 29 November. Nations Championship: Ireland fight back to earn bonus-point win over Fiji - reaction Fiji frustrate slow-starting Irish When these sides last met, in Dublin two years ago, Ireland scored four converted tries to effectively end the contest by half-time on their way to a 52-17 win. But this was anything but simple. Despite making seven changes from last week's victory over the Pumas and losing centre Jamie Osborne to an early injury, Ireland threatened to gallop into the distance in a hurry. The back three of Hansen, Baloucoune and O'Brien connected to put the latter in for an eighth-minute try - the wing atoning for an earlier knock-on. Gibson-Park, back in the starting line-up, thought he had added a second for Ireland, but the scrum-half lost control of the ball as he touched down. From there, Fiji decided to get moving and hit back quickly when mountainous centre Tuisova barged over the line after a piercing carry by Yato. Yato, who took over the captaincy from Tevita Ikanivere for Saturday's game, then touched down himself after winger Juta Wainiqolo surged through a hole in the home defence. Irish frustration deepened when Ryan Baird was stopped just short of the line but, after a superb Prendergast kick caused havoc in the Fijian defence, the fly-half put Baloucoune in after good work from the impressive Hansen. Fiji, playing with rising confidence, responded when prop Luke Tagi burst over, but Isoa Nasilasila was adjudged to have knocked the ball in the away side's line-out. But Ireland were further vexed before half-time amid an increasingly uneasy atmosphere at Aviva Stadium when Baloucoune's second try was followed by a yellow card for captain Tadhg Beirne - after Angus Gardner had initially shown a card to James Ryan. That allowed Volavola to kick the visitors to within two points at half-time. Hard-carrying James McNabney made a big impression on a debut that lasted only four minutes [Getty Images] Fiji - now coached by Jake White, who led South Africa to World Cup success in 2007 - played with immense physicality and purpose in the first half but their challenge faded after the restart. After Kelleher's try extended the home side's advantage, Ulster forward James McNabney made a stunning debut cameo off the bench. Within a few minutes of being introduced, the totemic 23-year-old rampaged through the Fijian defence and was stopped short by prop Inoke Ravuiwasa, who was yellow carded. McNabney, though, was unable to continue following the collision, but O'Brien, Porter and Timoney claimed later tries to add gloss to the scoreline. Ireland must now beat the Springboks next week and hope France and England slip up against Argentina and New Zealand to secure a berth in the final. Line-ups Ireland: Mack Hansen; Rob Baloucoune, Jamie Osborne, Bundee Aki, Tommy O'Brien; Sam Prendergast, Jamison Gibson-Park; Andrew Porter, Ronan Kelleher, Tadhg Furlong, James Ryan, Tadhg Beirne (capt), Ryan Baird, Josh van der Flier, Nick Timoney. Replacements: Tom Stewart, Tom O'Toole, Sam Illo, Darragh Murray, James McNabney, Craig Casey, Ciaran Frawley, Stuart McCloskey. Sin-bin: Beirne (41) Fiji: Ponipate Loganimasi; Selestino Ravutaumada, Setareki Bituniyata, Josua Tuisova, Jiuta Wainiqolo; Ben Volavola, Frank Lomani; Peni Ravai, Tevita Ikanivere, Luke Tagi, Joseva Tamani, Isoa Nasilasila, Mesake Vocevoce, Lekima Tagitagivalu, Peceli Yato (capt). Replacements: Zuriel Togiatama, Vilikesa Nairau, Inoke Ravuiwasa, Kitione Salawa, Elia Canakaivata, Terio Tamani, Caleb Muntz, Iosefo Masi. Sin-bin: Ravuiwasa (53) Referee: Angus Gardner (Aus)

item.title: Rams Week 10 injury report vs. Cardinals: Puka Nacua is on IR, so who will step up for LA?
item.description: Image Credit: David Brytus-Imagn Images Rams Week 10 injury report vs. Cardinals: Puka Nacua is on IR, so who will step up for LA? appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Rams enter their Week 10 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals facing a significant offensive adjustment. Puka Nacua is on injured reserve after suffering knee and toe injuries against Washington, leaving Matthew Stafford without the receiver who powered last Sunday’s passing attack. Nacua caught 14 passes for 150 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ 20-13 victory, drawing 19 targets. Replacing that involvement will require more than promoting one receiver. With Davante Adams and Jordan Whittington also on IR, Los Angeles must redistribute opportunities across a depleted group. The encouraging news is Stafford’s availability. Despite appearing on the injury report with a right elbow issue, he practiced fully throughout the week and carries no game designation. The challenge now is finding reliable answers around him. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Tyler Higbee leads the options to replace Puka Nacua’s production Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Tyler Higbee stands out as the main weapon to build around in Nacua’s absence, particularly on intermediate routes and crucial possession downs. His experience with Stafford makes him a logical candidate for additional attention, although that projection should not be mistaken for an announced target distribution. Higbee’s own health briefly complicated that outlook. An illness kept him out Thursday before he returned for limited work Friday. He received no game designation, leaving him available for an offense that needs dependable receiving options. The tight end group’s other injuries make his role especially important. Terrance Ferguson is out with ankle and hamstring injuries, while Davis Allen is questionable with an oblique issue. Colby Parkinson offers another available option after progressing to full participation Friday despite injured ribs. Tutu Atwell can provide a different dimension outside. His ability to threaten downfield offers a way to discourage Arizona from crowding shorter routes. Stafford connected with him for a 40-yard gain against the Chargers in Week 8, demonstrating the explosive element available beyond the depleted starting group. Konata Mumpfield also has an opportunity to earn a larger share of the passing game. He already produced a 48-yard touchdown reception against Denver earlier this season, giving Los Angeles another receiver with evidence of big-play potential. Consistency, rather than one explosive catch, becomes the next requirement. CJ Daniels Jr., Xavier Smith and newly promoted Brennan Presley round out the available receiver group. The Rams placed Nacua on IR Thursday to create the roster opening for Presley; Nacua must miss at least four games, making this adjustment more than a one-week assignment. Rams injury report in

Rams injury report includes key offensive and defensive questions Beyond Nacua’s absence, Steve Avila is ruled out after missing every practice with a hamstring injury. Losing an offensive lineman adds another complication as the Rams reshape their passing attack, especially if Stafford needs extra time for unfamiliar combinations to develop. Final Rams injury report vs. the Cardinals. TE Davis Allen – Questionable LS Joe Cardona – Questionable EDGE Myles Garrett – Questionable CB Trent McDuffie – Questionable S Kam Curl – Questionable LG Steve Avila – Out TE Terrance Ferguson – Out pic.twitter.com/qq3OM1bhAg — Blaine Grisak (@BGMediaOnSI) November 13, 2026 Allen’s questionable designation follows limited practices Wednesday and Friday around a missed Thursday session. Long snapper Joe Cardona is also questionable after remaining limited throughout the week with an ankle injury. Defensively, Myles Garrett carries a questionable designation for a knee issue and rest. He was limited Wednesday and Thursday before sitting out Friday. His availability matters after a three-sack performance against Washington helped Los Angeles secure its third consecutive victory. Trent McDuffie and Kam Curl are questionable, too. Both returned for limited work Friday after two missed sessions, managing back and toe injuries, respectively. Braden Fiske missed Friday with an ankle injury but received no game designation. Byron Young and Aaron Donald also sat out for rest without designations, distinguishing their absences from confirmed injury-related setbacks. item.title: Chargers’ Ladd McConkey gets official injury status for MNF vs. Ravens
item.description: Mark Konezny-Imagn Images Chargers’ Ladd McConkey gets official injury status for MNF vs. Ravens appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Chargers could be without one of their key receiving options when they visit the Baltimore Ravens on Monday night. Wide receiver Ladd McConkey has officially been listed as questionable because of a back injury , leaving his availability uncertain heading into the matchup. According to ESPN’s Adam Schefter, McConkey received the questionable designation on the Chargers’ latest injury report. The second-year receiver did not participate in Thursday or Friday’s practices as he continued dealing with the issue. McConkey’s back problems first became noticeable before Los Angeles’ Week 9 game. He was active for the matchup against the Houston Texans but did not take the field because of back spasms. His limited involvement during the team’s preparations for Baltimore adds another concern ahead of Monday’s kickoff. The Chargers will likely make a final decision closer to game time. McConkey’s status could remain uncertain until the team releases its inactive list, which typically comes around 90 minutes before kickoff. If he cannot play, or is available only in an emergency role, Quentin Johnston , Tre Harris and KeAndre Lambert-Smith could handle larger responsibilities in the passing game. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) There is some positive news for Los Angeles, as Harris has been cleared from the injury report and is no longer carrying a game designation. His availability would give quarterback Justin Herbert another option if McConkey misses the contest. Ladd McConkey has recorded 17 receptions for 286 yards and one touchdown across six games this season. His absence would be a notable setback for the Chargers as they prepare for a difficult road test against Baltimore. Related: NFL trade deadline ‘snafus’ has league competition committee considering potential changes Related: NFL announces changes made to Week 10 slate due to FAA ground stop

item.title: Miami 36, Duke 25: Five Key Plays
item.description: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 14: Javain Mallory #21 of the Miami Hurricanes rushes forward during the first half of the college football game against the Duke Blue Devils at Hard Rock Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Eston Parker/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images) | ISI Photos via Getty Images D uke fell to 7-3 (4-3) on the season with a 36-25 loss to the Miami Hurricanes. Nate Sheppard rushed 16 times for 131 yards and two touchdowns, and caught 12 passes for 93 yards in a tremendous performance. Walker Eget completed 26 of 42 pass attempts for 195 yards, one touchdown and one costly interception. The Blue Devils defense played the ‘Canes tough before wearing down in the 4th quarter. The halftime score was Miami 13, Duke 10 and it was Miami 22, Duke 17 at the end of the 3rd quarter. Miami won time of possession 34:13 to 25:47 and outgained Duke 532 to 341 in total yards. Miami quarterback Darian Mensah completed 30 of 41 pass attempts for 382 yards and one touchdown. Wide receiver Cooper Barkate was the ‘Canes leading receiver with eight receptions for 134 yards. Javian Mallory rushed 10 times for 71 yards and two touchdowns, and grabbed three receptions for 79 yards and a touchdown. Play One: Trailing 29-17, with 6 minutes and 54 seconds remaining in the game, Duke faced a 2nd down and nine yards to go at their own 46-yard line. Eget threw a pass down the right sideline toward Brody Keefe, but the pass was intercepted by Miami defensive back Xavier Lucas. Five plays later, Javian Mallory dashed 39 yards for a touchdown to expand Miami’s lead to 36-17. Play Two: With two minutes and 43 seconds remaining in the 3rd quarter, with the score 16-10 Miami, the ‘Canes had the ball on their own 37 yard line. Mensah completed a screen pass to Javian Mallory who rambled 63 yards for a touchdown to expand the lead to 22-10. The 2-point conversion attempt failed. Play Three: With Miami leading 10-3, on 1st down and 10, Sheppard exploded on an inside run for 47 yards and a touchdown, to tie the game at 10 points apiece. Play Four: On 2nd down and goal to go, with 41 seconds remaining in the 3rd quarter, Sheppard ran five yards for a touchdown to cut Miami’s lead to 22-17. Duke moved into scoring position two plays earlier when Duke executed a double pass from Eget to Sheppard to Javen Nicholas for 13 yards to the Miami 5-yard line. Sheppard rushed for 47 yards on the first play of the drive. Play Five: Duke’s stout defense kept the Blue Devils in the game. Three times Miami drove into the red zone, but settled for field goals instead of touchdowns, due to Duke getting stops on 3rd down. Two of the three times the stop came on 3rd down and goal to go. item.title: Weather moves up Round 4 of Austin Championship. Here's how to watch
item.description: The final round of the 2026 Austin Championship has been moved up due to inclement weather expected on Sunday. Golf Channel’s will start its Round 4 coverage at 12:30 p.m. ET with a half-hour Golf Central Pregame airing before. Trace Crowe emerged over a crowded leaderboard on Saturday that included Sami Valmaki, Erik van Rooyen and Chad Ramey. All three moved into contention on Moving Day but Crowe’s birdie-birdie finish gave him the leading score at 14 under. The 30-year-old Auburn grad is seeking his first win on Tour after breaking the course record with an opening round 62 on Thursday. Below are the final round groupings and tee times on Sunday at Fazio Canyons: "I've been doing this long enough to know that everyone's really good and they're just going to keep making birdies," Crowe said after the third round. "My mindset tomorrow is to go attack the day and see what it gives, but just try to play the best I can and hopefully it come out on top." Austin Championship - Final Rd The Austin Championship tees off at Omni Barton Creek Resort & Spa in Austin, Texas.

The Seattle Seahawks will be without Leonard Williams against the Las Vegas Raiders , removing a major defensive obstacle for Fernando Mendoza ahead of his first NFL start. Williams missed every practice this week with a stinger and was officially ruled out Friday, leaving Seattle to adjust its defensive front for Sunday’s matchup. His absence is one of four confirmed setbacks for the Seahawks. Quarterback Sam Darnold, left tackle Charles Cross and guard Quenton Nelson are also out, creating challenges on both sides of the ball as Seattle heads to Las Vegas. Seahawks injury report for Thursday Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Charles Cross practices as LIMITED No other real changes pic.twitter.com/cViKsMKQKA — Brian Nemhauser (@hawkblogger) November 12, 2026 For Mendoza, Williams’ unavailability represents a favorable development rather than a guarantee of an easier afternoon. Seattle still has defensive personnel capable of disrupting the rookie, but losing an established interior presence changes the protection equation. Leonard Williams ’ absence gives Fernando Mendoza breathing room Credit: Amber Searls-Imagn Images Williams’ recovery has not progressed enough for a return to contact. Head coach Mike Macdonald explained Friday that the defensive tackle can move around and maintain his conditioning, but the injury remains an obstacle to playing. “It’s one of those things where it’s not good until it is. It’s not good yet,” Macdonald said. “Stingers are more of a contact thing.” He added that Williams remains involved in meetings while working to stay fresh. That leaves Mendoza with one fewer disruptive defender to account for in his starting debut. The Raiders opened the door for the No. 1 overall pick by trading Kirk Cousins to Minnesota this week, making Sunday the beginning of a new chapter at quarterback. From a matchup standpoint, Williams’ absence could help Las Vegas maintain a cleaner pocket through the middle. Interior penetration can force a quarterback off his spot before routes develop, complicating reads and reducing throwing space. Avoiding those disruptions would help Mendoza settle into his first start. Seattle, however, views the unfamiliar quarterback as a preparation challenge of its own. Defensive tackle Byron Murphy II noted the limited professional film available on Mendoza while emphasizing that the rookie can make every throw. Murphy stressed coordinated pressure and communication as priorities. The Seahawks received encouraging news elsewhere up front. Uchenna Nwosu progressed from two limited sessions to full participation Friday and carries no game designation. Head coach Mike Macdonald explained Friday that the defensive tackle can move around and maintain his conditioning, but the injury remains an obstacle to playing. “It’s one of those things where it’s not good until it is. It’s not good yet,” Macdonald said. “Stingers are more of a contact thing.” He added that Williams remains involved in meetings while working to stay fresh. That leaves Mendoza with one fewer disruptive defender to account for in his starting debut. The Raiders opened the door for the No. 1 overall pick by trading Kirk Cousins to Minnesota this week, making Sunday the beginning of a new chapter at quarterback. From a matchup standpoint, Williams’ absence could help Las Vegas maintain a cleaner pocket through the middle. Interior penetration can force a quarterback off his spot before routes develop, complicating reads and reducing throwing space. Avoiding those disruptions would help Mendoza settle into his first start. Seattle, however, views the unfamiliar quarterback as a preparation challenge of its own. Defensive tackle Byron Murphy II noted the limited professional film available on Mendoza while emphasizing that the rookie can make every throw. Murphy stressed coordinated pressure and communication as priorities. The Seahawks received encouraging news elsewhere up front. Uchenna Nwosu progressed from two limited sessions to full participation Friday and carries no game designation. Brandon Pili also returned to full work after missing Wednesday and Thursday with a back injury, providing available depth without replacing Williams’ individual impact. Seahawks injury report leaves offense facing significant adjustments Darnold missed all three practices with rib and quadriceps injuries. Drew Lock is expected to start again despite managing right elbow and oblique issues. Lock remained limited throughout the week but received no game designation. Protecting him becomes more complicated without Cross and Nelson. Cross briefly returned for limited work Thursday before sitting out Friday with his ankle injury. Nelson did not practice all week because of his knee issue. Anthony Bradford offered better news, advancing to full participation Friday after two limited sessions. At receiver, Rashid Shaheed practiced fully throughout the week despite a knee injury. Jaxon Smith-Njigba returned to full work Thursday and Friday after Wednesday’s rest day. Neither has a game designation. The remaining defensive updates were largely positive. Patrick O’Connell and Connor O’Toole finished with full practices after earlier limitations. Jarran Reed returned Friday following two personal absences. Derick Hall missed Friday after two limited sessions with a back injury, but he also carries no game designation. That distinction leaves Seattle with four confirmed absences and no additional players officially listed as questionable. item.title: Akron basketball will benefit if Buddy Hammer Jr. can harness fire. Opinion
item.description: In one fell swoop, the University of Akron 's Buddy Hammer Jr. received a massive compliment and a decent dose of discipline from Zips men's basketball coach Dustin Ford on Saturday, Nov. 14. "I made up my mind I was willing to lose the game to hopefully teach him a lesson for down the road," Ford said. Ford benched Hammer after the senior forward drew a technical foul with 12:24 left in the second half against Tulane. Hammer had been dominating for the Zips, but Ford never put him back in the game. Hammer's foul and subsequent technical gave Tulane four foul shots, sparking the Green Wave's 14-0 run and rally from an 11-point deficit. In the end, Akron defeated Tulane 65-63, allowing Hammer to learn and Ford to hold a standout player accountable as the Zips (3-0) extended their winning streak at Rhodes Arena to 33 games. Akron wing Evan Mahaffey made the game-winning layup with 55.5 seconds remaining. Tulane guard KJ Greene drove for a layup of his own in the final seconds, yet his attempt missed. Akron's scoring leader with 17 points, guard Ty Pence secured the final rebound just before the buzzer. Hammer could let out a sigh of relief. During a postgame news conference, he broached the subject of his punishment before anyone asked about it. "I made a big mistake tonight. I let my team down in that moment," Hammer said. So what exactly did Hammer do to lose playing time against Tulane (2-2)? Hammer appeared to have ideal defensive position when the officials whistled him for a foul as he guarded Greene on another drive earlier in the second half. Hammer appeared to be frustrated with the call. He got his right hand on the ball, bouncing it hard off the floor and high into the air. Four successful free throws ensued. "I just thought I had good position," Hammer said. "It really wasn't I was mad at the ref or nothing like that. I just made a simple mistake, and I seen the ball, so I slapped it just for the heck of it. But it wasn't nothing. I wasn't real mad or nothing like that. And I told coach that, but in the moment and me doing that, it doesn't show how I was feeling. "Making that mistake, I know I just got to bounce back from that and learn from that because I can't be letting my team down like that, especially in tough moments. It was a four-point possession right there, so I can't be doing that and giving the team free throws and free points. We can't be doing that. We've just got to make sure we [maintain] mental toughness and being able to move on to the next play. OK, he called the foul. Let's keep going now." item.content:encoded: In one fell swoop, the University of Akron 's Buddy Hammer Jr. received a massive compliment and a decent dose of discipline from Zips men's basketball coach Dustin Ford on Saturday, Nov. 14. "I made up my mind I was willing to lose the game to hopefully teach him a lesson for down the road," Ford said. Ford benched Hammer after the senior forward drew a technical foul with 12:24 left in the second half against Tulane. Hammer had been dominating for the Zips, but Ford never put him back in the game. Hammer's foul and subsequent technical gave Tulane four foul shots, sparking the Green Wave's 14-0 run and rally from an 11-point deficit. In the end, Akron defeated Tulane 65-63, allowing Hammer to learn and Ford to hold a standout player accountable as the Zips (3-0) extended their winning streak at Rhodes Arena to 33 games. Akron wing Evan Mahaffey made the game-winning layup with 55.5 seconds remaining. Tulane guard KJ Greene drove for a layup of his own in the final seconds, yet his attempt missed. Akron's scoring leader with 17 points, guard Ty Pence secured the final rebound just before the buzzer. Hammer could let out a sigh of relief. During a postgame news conference, he broached the subject of his punishment before anyone asked about it. "I made a big mistake tonight. I let my team down in that moment," Hammer said. So what exactly did Hammer do to lose playing time against Tulane (2-2)? Hammer appeared to have ideal defensive position when the officials whistled him for a foul as he guarded Greene on another drive earlier in the second half. Hammer appeared to be frustrated with the call. He got his right hand on the ball, bouncing it hard off the floor and high into the air. Four successful free throws ensued. "I just thought I had good position," Hammer said. "It really wasn't I was mad at the ref or nothing like that. I just made a simple mistake, and I seen the ball, so I slapped it just for the heck of it. But it wasn't nothing. I wasn't real mad or nothing like that. And I told coach that, but in the moment and me doing that, it doesn't show how I was feeling. "Making that mistake, I know I just got to bounce back from that and learn from that because I can't be letting my team down like that, especially in tough moments. It was a four-point possession right there, so I can't be doing that and giving the team free throws and free points. We can't be doing that. We've just got to make sure we [maintain] mental toughness and being able to move on to the next play. OK, he called the foul. Let's keep going now." On the surface, the penalty Hammer received from Ford seemed to be too harsh for smacking the ball. But Ford pointed out Hammer also picked up a technical earlier in the week during a 112-64 victory over Muskingum. There was a pattern by the player and a method to the first-year college head coach's madness. "He plays with emotion and passion, and I coach with emotion and passion," Ford said. "I'm probably going to lose my mind at times, too. But you can't get a technical foul in that juncture. He's had that issue, and I want to get that cleaned up, but I also don't want the kid beating himself up. "There are going to be some games with a lot more emotion than there was in there [against Tulane]. He's got to be able to channel that [emotion] because he's a smart kid." When teams essentially start over every season during an era of college sports shaped by name, image and likeness deals and the NCAA transfer portal, how is a coach supposed to establish a culture? Give Ford credit for trying, even though he took a risk as part of the big-picture mission. A transfer from the University of North Texas, Hammer compiled 11 points on 5-of-6 shooting from the field (0 of 1 on 3-pointers), six rebounds, two assists and two steals in 17 minutes off the bench. His motor is relentless, and Akron had firm control when he was in the game. Without Hammer, the Zips found themselves in jeopardy of losing for the first time at home since March 5, 2024. "With about five minutes to go, I started second-guessing myself, and the [assistant] coaches were in my ear [about benching Hammer], but I tried to stick to it," Ford conceded. This is how Ford complimented Hammer through actions, not words: The coach would not have gone through the trouble of making an example of the player during a game unless the coach had significant plans for the player this season. Hammer's elite level of energy and hustle is unmatched among Zips players since UA legend Enrique Freeman entered the NBA and NBA G League. In a span of 21 seconds in the first half, Hammer dived for a loose ball, almost inadvertently causing an official to wipe out near Akron's bench, and took a charge from Tulane forward Joah Chappelle. Hammer has Zips fan favorite and Mid-American Conference Sixth Man of the Year candidacy written all over him. "If I could get on NBA Live and craft a player, I'd want [one like Hammer]," Ford said. "[He] just plays hard. And I think if we can keep him out of foul trouble and keep him from some things like that [technical], he's a guy that could be a double-double guy. No doubt about it, and then he could be extremely efficient while he's doing it." Akron forward Halil "Chabi" Barre, who had five points and a game-high 10 rebounds, injected some humor into the situation when he was asked to describe what Hammer has brought to the Zips. "Technical fouls," Barre said with a smile, causing Hammer to laugh while sitting next to him. Barre continued, "He's probably one of the toughest guys on the team. He brings huge energy on both sides of the court and obviously rebounding." As Akron seeks its fourth consecutive MAC Tournament title, the team will need Hammer on the court to reach its potential this season. UA wears a gigantic target on its back, and showdowns against Kent State, Miami, Toledo, among others, are sure to be intense. If Hammer were better equipped to harness his competitive fire in those moments, he and Ford would be able to look back at Akron versus Tulane as a turning point. Nate Ulrich is the sports columnist of the Akron Beacon Journal and a sports features writer. Nate can be reached at nulrich@thebeaconjournal.com . On Twitter: @ByNateUlrich . item.title: Brad Holmes Fires Back at Critics Over Detroit Lions Trade Deadline Decisions
item.description: Detroit Lions general manager Brad Holmes has heard the criticism about his approach to the NFL trade deadline, and he has a message for anyone who believes the team has become complacent. He’s not buying it. Not even a little bit. During an exclusive interview with Colton Pouncy of The Athletic , Holmes addressed concerns that Detroit failed to do enough to improve its roster before Tuesday’s deadline. While other NFC contenders made aggressive moves, the Lions added veteran safety Andre Cisco from the New York Jets and decided against making another major trade. That decision has sparked plenty of criticism , but Holmes made it clear that a lack of headline-grabbing transactions does not mean the organization isn’t working to get better. Detroit Lions general manager Brad Holmes arrives at Northwest Stadium before the win against the Washington Commanders in Landover, Md. on Sunday, Nov. 9, 2025. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Brad Holmes Responds to Complacency Criticism When asked directly about fans who believe the Lions have become complacent, Holmes didn’t hold back. “Complacency doesn’t exist in our process,” Holmes said. “We made the moves that we made because we got a player that we liked on a deal. Whatever we did, it’s not indicative of our work ethic or complacency or our process. The trade deadline happens to have a title on it, but it’s really not any other different week besides — you might get an uptick in phone calls, but we’re calling and working the phones all year. Like, we’re doing this stuff in August and September, October. We’re doing this all the time, year-round. So, there’s no complacency. Nobody’s in position to be complacent. You’ve probably heard me say multiple times, I never think it’s enough. No matter how talented our roster gets, it’s never enough. And once you think it’s enough, that’s when you’ll get beat. So, there’s never complacency.” Holmes wasn’t finished, either. He emphasized that Detroit will not make a trade simply to satisfy people outside the organization. “But we’re also — we’re not going to make a move just to make a move to satisfy somebody outside of what we’re doing. We’re going to do what’s right for us, and we’re also going to do what we can do. We’re not going to add a player that we’re not excited about or doesn’t make a lot of sense or is going to compromise us in a certain way.” That’s a pretty clear message from Detroit’s general manager, especially considering the pressure surrounding the team’s championship aspirations. item.content:encoded: Detroit Lions general manager Brad Holmes has heard the criticism about his approach to the NFL trade deadline, and he has a message for anyone who believes the team has become complacent. He’s not buying it. Not even a little bit. During an exclusive interview with Colton Pouncy of The Athletic , Holmes addressed concerns that Detroit failed to do enough to improve its roster before Tuesday’s deadline. While other NFC contenders made aggressive moves, the Lions added veteran safety Andre Cisco from the New York Jets and decided against making another major trade. That decision has sparked plenty of criticism , but Holmes made it clear that a lack of headline-grabbing transactions does not mean the organization isn’t working to get better. Detroit Lions general manager Brad Holmes arrives at Northwest Stadium before the win against the Washington Commanders in Landover, Md. on Sunday, Nov. 9, 2025. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Brad Holmes Responds to Complacency Criticism When asked directly about fans who believe the Lions have become complacent, Holmes didn’t hold back. “Complacency doesn’t exist in our process,” Holmes said. “We made the moves that we made because we got a player that we liked on a deal. Whatever we did, it’s not indicative of our work ethic or complacency or our process. The trade deadline happens to have a title on it, but it’s really not any other different week besides — you might get an uptick in phone calls, but we’re calling and working the phones all year. Like, we’re doing this stuff in August and September, October. We’re doing this all the time, year-round. So, there’s no complacency. Nobody’s in position to be complacent. You’ve probably heard me say multiple times, I never think it’s enough. No matter how talented our roster gets, it’s never enough. And once you think it’s enough, that’s when you’ll get beat. So, there’s never complacency.” Holmes wasn’t finished, either. He emphasized that Detroit will not make a trade simply to satisfy people outside the organization. “But we’re also — we’re not going to make a move just to make a move to satisfy somebody outside of what we’re doing. We’re going to do what’s right for us, and we’re also going to do what we can do. We’re not going to add a player that we’re not excited about or doesn’t make a lot of sense or is going to compromise us in a certain way.” That’s a pretty clear message from Detroit’s general manager, especially considering the pressure surrounding the team’s championship aspirations. Holmes understands the expectations, but he isn’t about to abandon his approach just because another team makes a splash. Holmes Still Believes Lions Are Heading in Right Direction The Lions acquired Cisco ahead of the deadline , but fans hoping for additional help at cornerback or linebacker were left disappointed. Holmes, however, believes the current roster is improving and still has room to grow. “Look, we have a hungry football team that is still growing, and we’re on the right track,” Holmes said. “I believe that our offense is really talented, very explosive. I think there’s still meat on the bone there and then I think our defense is gaining confidence by the week. I just think that’s just a culmination of the players taking ownership and the coaches putting the players in the right position and maximizing the personnel that we do have. “But we will never rest on our laurels. We will never think anything is good enough. We’re always gonna look inwards and look for ways to improve. That’s what we’ve always done, and we’ll continue to do.” Holmes has helped build a Lions team that has gone from one of the NFL’s perennial disappointments to a legitimate contender. His commitment to developing talent and protecting future assets has been central to that turnaround, even if his conservative approach to the trade deadline has frustrated some fans. But there is another side to the argument, and it’s a fair one. Detroit has a roster capable of competing for a championship right now, and some fans understandably wonder whether a more aggressive move could have improved the Lions’ chances of finally winning a Super Bowl. For Holmes, the answer isn’t about winning the trade deadline or making the loudest move. It’s about making decisions he believes give Detroit the best chance to succeed, both now and in the future. Whether that approach proves correct remains to be seen. One thing is certain, though: Brad Holmes isn’t apologizing for how he handled the deadline.

item.title: Michigan QB Bryce Underwood replaces Tommy Carr after difficult start vs. Oregon
item.description: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images Michigan QB Bryce Underwood replaces Tommy Carr after difficult start vs. Oregon appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Michigan football rolled with a new play-caller for Tommy Carr before facing the Oregon Ducks . But coach Kyle Whittingham pivoted back to Bryce Underwood Saturday. All because of Carr’s rough start post Jason Beck firing as offensive coordinator . Carr got pulled after posting these disastrous numbers: 1-of-5 for eight yards. Michigan needed to lean into the ground game to produce any kind of offense in Eugene. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) So running back Savion Hiter tallied 71 yards on just two carries. Jordan Marshall added 14 yards with two carries. But Oregon jumped on the Wolverines early with a 14-7 lead. Featuring Ducks quarterback Dylan Raiola exposing the Michigan secondary with a 60-yard touchdown lob to Jeremiah McClellan. Raiola added a shorter two-yarder that built the Ducks lead to 14-0. Hiter, though, sliced through the Oregon defense on a 70-yard scoring scamper that cut the deficit to 14-7. Michigan still has endured a tumultuous season in year one of the Whittingham era. The Wolverines started by escaping Western Michigan with an Underwood Hail Mary that involved a controversial play clock debate. Michigan later pulled Underwood from behind center amid some notable struggles on offense during the time Beck was calling the offense. Which swung the starting spot over to Carr. Carr gets pulled now amid his own slow start as “Whitt” turns back to Underwood. Michigan is aiming to install any kind of momentum. Especially after absorbing the brutal 15-6 loss to struggling Michigan State one week ago. Yet the Wolverines need just one victory to become bowl eligible at 5-4 overall. Related: Oregon’s Dylan Raiola connects with Dakorien Moore for electric TD vs. Michigan Related: Ohio State’s Ryan Day gives in-depth analysis of Jeremiah Smith’s Heisman argument

item.title: No. 6 Texas at No. 21 LSU live updates: Horns try to overcome travel issues
item.description: Nothing about this weekend was ever going to be easy — going into Death Valley and attempting to beat the supremely talented No. 21 LSU Tigers at night in the sixth conference game in six weeks for the No. 6 Texas Longhorns, who have already secured wins against four other ranked opponents. But Friday’s shocking FAA ground stop threw everything into chaos. Just as the Longhorns were set to depart Austin, the order forced Steve Sarkisian’s team to deplane and return to campus for a meal, walk-though, and meetings before the plane was finally able to depart seven hours late. By the time Texas got to its team hotel in Baton Rouge, it was past midnight. Now it’s up to a team that Sarkisian lauded for its undeniable toughness last week to turn that inconvenience into a historical footnote instead of an excuse. Able to keep their Saturday schedule, the Horns expect to perform well at Tiger Stadium, according to ESPN’s Holly Rowe. Here's an inside look to the struggled Texas had to deal with to get to Baton Rouge with the FAA ground stop pic.twitter.com/bUgIMeKlF1 — Nash (@NashTalksTexas) November 14, 2026 With a win, Texas has a 95-percent chance to return to the College Football Playoff . With a loss? Down to 60 percent. Those are the stakes on Saturday.

item.title: FINAL: TCU Horned Frogs 20, K-State Wildcats 10
item.description: Dillon Duff has developed an effective working relationship with tight end Garrett Oakley (as well as wide receiver Jaron Tibbs). | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images A defensive struggle for the most part, marred by two Kansas State turnovers, led to yet another defeat for the visiting Wildcats as they fell 20-10 to the TCU Horned Frogs this afternoon at Amon Carter Stadium in Fort Worth, Texas. K-State (4-6, 1-6 Big 12) made some progress with their shaky run defense today, but a key fumble early in the game led to an early TCU (3-4, 5-5 Big 12) touchdown, and the Frogs shut down the Wildcat running game well enough to prevent the Cats from mounting an effective comeback. The Cats got to midfield before having to punt on the opening drive, then forced a 3-and-out. But Rodney Fields fumbled at the Wildcat 28 and TCU recovered; three plays later, Kari Ashley took a direct snap and raced 19 yards to put TCU on the board first. Both teams went 3-and-out, then the Cats managed one first down before punting; Jaden Craig then hit Jordan Dwyer for 41 yards into K-State territory. TCU had to settle for a 29-yard Kyle Lemmermann field goal as the defense managed to hold after that. K-State had to punt again, but on TCU’s drive sacks on first and third down by Kamari Burns and Jayden Bryant with Travis Bates forced yet another punt. Near midfield on 3rd-and-10, Duff’s inexperience led to another sack, and another punt, Simon McClannan’s fifth of the first half. As TCU drove, Darien Whitaker recorded the third Wildcat sack of the half, trapping TCU with a 3rd-and-15 at the 35; Burns and Bates combined for the fourth sack on the next play, pushing the Frogs back far enough to have to punt instead of attempting a field goal. But only 15 seconds remained in the half, and K-State just took a knee to reset. TCU drove well after the half, marching downfield and scoring on a 5-yard pass from Craig to Jacobe Hayes to make the score 17-0. On the ensuing drive, one 24-yard run by Joe Jackson nearly doubled the team’s entire rushing output on its own, getting K-State into TCU territory for the first time all afternoon. A 55-yard field goal by Luis Rodriguez — a career high — broke up the shutout. The Frogs got into Wildcat territory, but a pair of big stops inside the 40 left TCU in no-man’s land, and they had to punt. It wasn’t much of a gain, as the punt went into the end zone. Two plays later, Duff found Jaron Tibbs wide open for a 53-yard score to close the gap to 17-10. The defense gave ground, though, and the Frogs reached the red zone. But the Cats held there, forcing a 36-yard field goal by Lemmermann. A small victory, but it did make the game a two-score affair again. K-State moved the ball in response, but ended up having to punt. A quick 3-and-out got them the ball back again, but as the Cats marched toward the red zone, the offensive line got worked over, resulting in a 15-yard sack and a fumble by Duff, recovered near midfield with only 1:58 to play. item.content:encoded: Dillon Duff has developed an effective working relationship with tight end Garrett Oakley (as well as wide receiver Jaron Tibbs). | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images A defensive struggle for the most part, marred by two Kansas State turnovers, led to yet another defeat for the visiting Wildcats as they fell 20-10 to the TCU Horned Frogs this afternoon at Amon Carter Stadium in Fort Worth, Texas. K-State (4-6, 1-6 Big 12) made some progress with their shaky run defense today, but a key fumble early in the game led to an early TCU (3-4, 5-5 Big 12) touchdown, and the Frogs shut down the Wildcat running game well enough to prevent the Cats from mounting an effective comeback. The Cats got to midfield before having to punt on the opening drive, then forced a 3-and-out. But Rodney Fields fumbled at the Wildcat 28 and TCU recovered; three plays later, Kari Ashley took a direct snap and raced 19 yards to put TCU on the board first. Both teams went 3-and-out, then the Cats managed one first down before punting; Jaden Craig then hit Jordan Dwyer for 41 yards into K-State territory. TCU had to settle for a 29-yard Kyle Lemmermann field goal as the defense managed to hold after that. K-State had to punt again, but on TCU’s drive sacks on first and third down by Kamari Burns and Jayden Bryant with Travis Bates forced yet another punt. Near midfield on 3rd-and-10, Duff’s inexperience led to another sack, and another punt, Simon McClannan’s fifth of the first half. As TCU drove, Darien Whitaker recorded the third Wildcat sack of the half, trapping TCU with a 3rd-and-15 at the 35; Burns and Bates combined for the fourth sack on the next play, pushing the Frogs back far enough to have to punt instead of attempting a field goal. But only 15 seconds remained in the half, and K-State just took a knee to reset. TCU drove well after the half, marching downfield and scoring on a 5-yard pass from Craig to Jacobe Hayes to make the score 17-0. On the ensuing drive, one 24-yard run by Joe Jackson nearly doubled the team’s entire rushing output on its own, getting K-State into TCU territory for the first time all afternoon. A 55-yard field goal by Luis Rodriguez — a career high — broke up the shutout. The Frogs got into Wildcat territory, but a pair of big stops inside the 40 left TCU in no-man’s land, and they had to punt. It wasn’t much of a gain, as the punt went into the end zone. Two plays later, Duff found Jaron Tibbs wide open for a 53-yard score to close the gap to 17-10. The defense gave ground, though, and the Frogs reached the red zone. But the Cats held there, forcing a 36-yard field goal by Lemmermann. A small victory, but it did make the game a two-score affair again. K-State moved the ball in response, but ended up having to punt. A quick 3-and-out got them the ball back again, but as the Cats marched toward the red zone, the offensive line got worked over, resulting in a 15-yard sack and a fumble by Duff, recovered near midfield with only 1:58 to play. TCU was able to kill the clock, and that was that. Duff was 22-33 for 244 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions. On the ground, he had 10 carries for a loss of seven yards and one fumble — but adjusted for sacks, that was actually 10 for 31. The Cats were terrible on the ground; Jackson (5 carries) and Fields (9) each had 33 yards. Tibbs and Garrett Oakley carried the weight in the air, Tibbs catching eight balls for 115 yards and a score, Oakley snagging six for 60. Derrick Salley had two catches for 32 yards, and Linkon Cure had two for 26. TCU outgained the Cats 324-302, outrushing K-State 99-58. The Wildcats did outgain the Frogs in the air 244-225. Penalties were a minor issue, K-State picking up four for 41 yards while TCU was only flagged once for ten. The Cats actually gained more yards per play, 5.2 to 4.7, but lost the turnover battle 2-0 and that may have ultimately been the deciding factor in the game. TCU led time of possession 32-28. WHAT WE… OBSERVED We didn’t learn much, because this team is irretrievably broken for the season thanks to injuries. But there were takeaways worth noting this week. 1) Whatever they did to work on run defense worked — today. TCU was held under 100 yards on the ground (although taking sack yardage into account it was 116 yards). Nearly half of that yardage came on a single play; subtract Payne’s 55-yard run and TCU was held to 61 yards otherwise. That’s worth noting, and good. (And four sacks? Gravy.) 2) Dillon Duff was the better quarterback in this game — indisputably. Duff wasn’t just the better of two bad quarterbacks, either. His passer rating on the day was 138.8, completing 2/3 of his passes, not making any egregious mistakes. He’s still shaky sometimes and runs himself into a sack, but he’s vastly improved over his first start, and showed progress over his relief appearance last week, in which he was also not bad at all. If he’s ultimately the future, he may have what it takes after all. 3) The offensive line, though. Oof. The line gave up five sacks today, which is almost 30% of the total allowed for the entire season . And they couldn’t run block to save their lives. It’s been an issue all year, off and on, especially in the eye test. Today, the numbers proved the hypothesis. PLAYERS OF THE GAME Have a hundred-yard day, be offensive player of the game, Jaron Tibbs . On defense, the four Wildcats who recorded full or partial sacks could’ve taken the honor, but Asa Newsom was everywhere today, recording 11 tackles, five solo, and was in on a tackle for loss. NEXT It doesn’t get any easier. #23 Arizona comes to town for the home finale, time and network yet to be determined.

item.title: Vikings make roster moves amid Jordan Addison’s injury concern
item.description: © Jeffrey Becker-Imagn Images Vikings make roster moves amid Jordan Addison’s injury concern appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Minnesota Vikings made a pair of roster moves Saturday as wide receiver Jordan Addison deals with a thumb injury ahead of a pivotal NFC North matchup against the Green Bay Packers . As the Vikings (6-2) prepare to face the Packers (6-3) on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox at Lambeau Field, Minnesota elevated tight end Devin Culp and wide receiver Jeshaun Jones to the active roster. The Vikings announced the moves Saturday on X, formerly known as Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “The #Vikings have elevated TE Devin Culp and WR Jeshaun Jones to the active roster for tomorrow’s game. “Culp has changed jersey numbers from 48 to 83.” The #Vikings have elevated TE Devin Culp and WR Jeshaun Jones to the active roster for tomorrow's game. Culp has changed jersey numbers from 48 to 83. pic.twitter.com/OU2Al6Oh0J — Minnesota Vikings (@Vikings) November 14, 2026 Jones’ elevation provides Minnesota with additional depth at wide receiver amid the injury concern surrounding Addison. The Vikings will hope to have their offensive weapons available for a divisional matchup that could have significant implications in the NFC North race. Vikings prepare for Packers with Kirk Cousins back in Minnesota Minnesota will also have a familiar face under center against Green Bay. Kirk Cousins will make his first start since returning to the Vikings after Minnesota acquired the veteran quarterback from the Las Vegas Raiders earlier this week in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick. Head coach Kevin O’Connell confirmed Friday that Cousins will immediately take over the starting role. Cousins previously played six seasons with Minnesota from 2018 through 2023 and spent two seasons working with O’Connell before leaving the organization. The Vikings enter Sunday’s matchup looking to end a two-game losing streak after beginning the season 6-0. Minnesota suffered a 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football in Week 9, marking its second consecutive defeat. Now, the Vikings will look to get back on track against a 6-3 Packers team while managing Addison’s injury status and integrating Cousins back into the offense. Related: Vikings’ biggest mistake at 2026 NFL Trade Deadline after adding Kirk Cousins Related: Vikings’ Blake Cashman, Kyler Murray headline ruled out players for Packers tilt

item.title: Girona makes a comeback in Oviedo and takes three golden points
item.description: Girona makes a comeback in Oviedo and takes three golden points Girona turned the score around at the Carlos Tartiere and defeated Oviedo 1-2. After a goalless first half, but with Girona dominating — they had 65% possession — the match became much more lively in the second half. Oviedo took the lead in the 47th minute with a goal from Reina, but Girona did not give up. In the 59th minute, Abel Ruiz equalized with an assist from Pyshchur. Five minutes later, in the 64th minute, Pyshchur completed the comeback: a ball remained in the area, and the forward stretched his leg to push it into the back of the net, securing the final 1-2 score. The victory allows Girona to reach 24 points. The next match will be on Sunday at Montilivi, at 6:30 PM, against Eibar.

item.title: Panthers S Zakee Wheatley fined for play vs. Broncos in Week 9
item.description: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images | Getty Images Panthers safety Zakee Wheatley has been fined $5,626 for a hit on a defenseless player in Carolina’s Week 9 loss to the Denver Broncos. The fine was assessed for a first-and-10 Broncos play with 19 seconds to play in the first quarter of Week 9. Marco Wilson was flagged for taunting on the same play, but Wheatley was not flagged at the time. It’s Wheatley’s second fine of the 2026 season. He was also fined $5,626 for taunting against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 6. No Denver players were fined for any plays in the Panthers’ 26-21 loss in Week 9. The NFL divides up the money it collects from player fines between the NFLPA’s efforts to support retired players, the NFL Foundation, and other nonprofits supporting youth sports, community health initiatives, and player health and safety at all levels of sports. The Panthers will face off against the New Orleans Saints on the road in Week 11.

item.title: Grand Slam of Darts: Schedule, results & prize money
item.description: Luke Littler became world number one for the first time when he won the Grand Slam of Darts in 2025 [Press Association] The 2026 Grand Slam of Darts gets under way on Saturday, as another of the Professional Darts Corporation's (PDC) major titles is set to be won in Wolverhampton. This edition is bigger than ever, with 48 players taking part, and unlike most of darts' major tournaments, the players are split into groups in the initial phase, rather than a straight knockout format. Each player will face two opponents in their group, with only the group winner progressing into the last 16. The rest of the competition is a straight knockout format. Luke Littler is the defending champion following a 16-11 victory over Luke Humphries in the 2025 final to become world number one for the first time. Littler faces a tough start, with Beau Greaves his opponent on the opening evening, and Neils Zonneveld, who beat Littler in their only previous meeting, completing the group. When is the Grand Slam of Darts? The tournament lasts for nine days from Saturday, 14 November to Sunday, 22 November. Group stage (14-17 November) - 48 matches Second round (18-19 November) - eight matches Quarter-finals (20-21 November) Semi-finals (22 November) Final (22 November) What is the format? In the group stage, the format is best of nine legs, or first to five legs. In the initial phase, two points are awarded for a win, with the group winner progressing to the last 16. In case of players being level on points at the end of the group phase, the following tie-breakers apply: Total Leg Difference Total Legs Won Total Legs Won Against Throw Highest Total Tournament Average (to two decimal places) Highest Winning Match Average (to two decimal places) A play-off - nine-dart leg Second-round matches are a best-of-19 format, or first to 10 legs. The quarter-finals, semi-finals and final are best of 31 legs, or first to 16 legs. Who is playing and how did they qualify? With the tournament expanded, a new set of qualification rules have been put in place. Up to 24 players could qualify from reaching a major PDC televised final in the past 12 months, but only nine ended up qualifying via that route, partly because of the dominance Littler has shown. Ten players reached Wolverhampton from the PDC youth, development and challenge tours, the Women's Matchplay and Women's Series and championships from across the globe. Six more secured places through the European Tour, while 13 qualified with a Players Championship win. The final 10 spots, which include ninth seed Stephen Bunting, were claimed in a PDC tour card holder qualifying event. From there, the top-16 ranked players in the PDC's order of merit were seeded and filled pot one. The next 16 went into pot two and the final 16 made up pot three. One player from each pot was then allocated to a group. Grand Slam of Darts groups, order of play & results Afternoon sessions start at 13:00 GMT, with evening sessions at 19:00 (19:30 on 15).

item.title: Takeaways from Maryland football’s 24-21 win over Wisconsin
item.description: After breaking its 13-game Big Ten losing streak, Maryland football had a chance to snap a pair of droughts against Wisconsin. The Terps hadn’t won consecutive Big Ten games since 2023 and were winless in their previous nine home conference clashes. Those skids came to an end Saturday. Even without starting quarterback Malik Washington, Maryland stormed back from a 10-point deficit to defeat Wisconsin, 24-21. Sean O’Haire drilled a 30-yard field goal with 29 seconds remaining to pull off the come-from-behind victory. Here are three takeaways from Saturday’s drubbing. Rejuvenated offense without Malik Washington During Washington’s early-season struggles, some fans called for a switch to backup quarterback Cardell Williams. Saturday was fans’ first real glimpse at what the Sacramento State transfer offered under center. Williams’ first start at Maryland was turbulent early on, despite operating with a simplified playbook. His first two pass completions were targeted to Chris Durr Jr. behind the line of scrimmage for just four combined yards. While offensive coordinator Clint Trickett’s play selection emphasized getting the ball to his weapons, it wasn’t successful. Williams’ nine-yard pass to Durr on Maryland’s third possession was the longest completion for the opening 23 minutes. The redshirt senior did show some promise, threading the needle between two Wisconsin defenders for a 30-yard gain to Preston Howard. Williams later punched it in for a one-yard rushing touchdown to cap off a methodical drive. While Williams’ accuracy was shaky early on, he looked more comfortable in the pocket after the first quarter. He finished with 183 passing yards on an efficient 21-for-23, including a program-record 19 consecutive completions. His 91.3% completion percentage was also a school-high. Without its starting quarterback, Maryland’s run game became more prevalent. Following a 99-yard rushing performance against Purdue, DeJuan Williams had 22 carries for 72 rushing yards. But 50 of those yards came in the second half, with gaping holes emerging. The bulk of the Terps’ success on the ground early on came via quarterback scrambles. Cardell Williams was the leading rusher in the first half with 22 yards and totaled a pair of rushing touchdowns in the game. “He’s special as far as what he can do with his feet,” head coach Aazaar Abdul-Rahim said. “We were excited that Wisconsin hadn’t played that type of quarterback this year. So we put in a lot of things that we were hoping to be successful with offensively.” Turnover battle aids success After producing seven sacks and 13 tackles for loss against Purdue, Maryland’s pass rush continued to get home Saturday. item.content:encoded: After breaking its 13-game Big Ten losing streak, Maryland football had a chance to snap a pair of droughts against Wisconsin. The Terps hadn’t won consecutive Big Ten games since 2023 and were winless in their previous nine home conference clashes. Those skids came to an end Saturday. Even without starting quarterback Malik Washington, Maryland stormed back from a 10-point deficit to defeat Wisconsin, 24-21. Sean O’Haire drilled a 30-yard field goal with 29 seconds remaining to pull off the come-from-behind victory. Here are three takeaways from Saturday’s drubbing. Rejuvenated offense without Malik Washington During Washington’s early-season struggles, some fans called for a switch to backup quarterback Cardell Williams. Saturday was fans’ first real glimpse at what the Sacramento State transfer offered under center. Williams’ first start at Maryland was turbulent early on, despite operating with a simplified playbook. His first two pass completions were targeted to Chris Durr Jr. behind the line of scrimmage for just four combined yards. While offensive coordinator Clint Trickett’s play selection emphasized getting the ball to his weapons, it wasn’t successful. Williams’ nine-yard pass to Durr on Maryland’s third possession was the longest completion for the opening 23 minutes. The redshirt senior did show some promise, threading the needle between two Wisconsin defenders for a 30-yard gain to Preston Howard. Williams later punched it in for a one-yard rushing touchdown to cap off a methodical drive. While Williams’ accuracy was shaky early on, he looked more comfortable in the pocket after the first quarter. He finished with 183 passing yards on an efficient 21-for-23, including a program-record 19 consecutive completions. His 91.3% completion percentage was also a school-high. Without its starting quarterback, Maryland’s run game became more prevalent. Following a 99-yard rushing performance against Purdue, DeJuan Williams had 22 carries for 72 rushing yards. But 50 of those yards came in the second half, with gaping holes emerging. The bulk of the Terps’ success on the ground early on came via quarterback scrambles. Cardell Williams was the leading rusher in the first half with 22 yards and totaled a pair of rushing touchdowns in the game. “He’s special as far as what he can do with his feet,” head coach Aazaar Abdul-Rahim said. “We were excited that Wisconsin hadn’t played that type of quarterback this year. So we put in a lot of things that we were hoping to be successful with offensively.” Turnover battle aids success After producing seven sacks and 13 tackles for loss against Purdue, Maryland’s pass rush continued to get home Saturday. The Terps pressured Wisconsin quarterback Ryan Hopkins eight times, with four leading to sacks. It wasn’t from Maryland’s typical players, though; Trey Redick, Jamare Glasker and Lavon Johnson each recorded a sack. Nahsir Taylor and Jayden Shipps teamed up for one late in the second quarter. But the impact of the pass rush also helped the Terps gain good starting field position for the offense. Maryland forced three fumbles, including Reddick’s strip sack that positioned Maryland at Wisconsin’s 33-yard line for the game-winning field goal. “We really didn’t have a lot of turnovers as we did last year,” Reddick said. “We had multiple turnovers, but we made an emphasis this game that we were going to have to win the game on defense, and that’s what we did. Had to force more turnovers than we did all year.” While the Terps didn’t convert on Johnson’s forced fumble in the first quarter — the offense stalled out after a pair of penalties — they scored 10 points off the final two turnovers. However, the Terps had their own costly fumble late in the first half. After driving down the field, Cardell Williams botched a handoff to Iverson Howard on the one-yard line. But that turnover didn’t prove costly, largely thanks to Maryland’s defense, which gave the offense five drives in Wisconsin territory. Backbreaking penalties While Maryland was flagged just once in Abdul-Rahim’s first game, the penalties have piled up in the last two weeks. The Terps were called for nine flags against Purdue, with Zion Elee’s personal foul aiding the Boilermakers potential game-winning drive. The freshman, who leads Maryland with six sacks, has committed multiple costly penalties this season. After not committing a penalty in the first four games, Elee has been flagged six times in the last six games. Three of those have been unsportsmanlike conducts along with a pair of personal fouls. The freshman has let his emotions get the best of him at points this season. “Unacceptable. First and foremost, not gonna be tolerated,” Abdul-Rahim said. “Immaturity at its best. [He] just turned 19 years old yesterday, and it’s not just him.” Elee had two of the Terps’ 11 penalties Saturday, with a roughing the kicker penalty that erased Wisconsin’s three-and-out. That prompted one of Maryland’s assistant coaches to pick up an unsportsmanlike conduct after arguing with the officials over the call. “Teachable moments are always better when you have a win behind,” Abdul-Rahim said. “So all of his teachable moments, we don’t accept that. Built on discipline.”

item.description: Wales produced the performance of the Nations Championship so far with a historic 35-28 victory over New Zealand at a raucous Principality Stadium on Saturday. In arguably the biggest shock in Test rugby since Japan beat South Africa in the 2015 World Cup, Wales defended heroically to claim their first win over the All Blacks since 1953. The win moved Wales into fourth place in the northern hemisphere standings, however, Scotland can leap back above Steve Tandy's side if they beat Australia on Sunday. New Zealand might have lost for the first time in the new championship but they still went top of the southern hemisphere pool after securing a bonus point. They lead South Africa by one point heading into the final round of group games next Saturday, with the All Blacks facing England and the Springboks taking on Ireland. France ended South Africa's 100% record with a sensational 21-19 victory over the world champions at the Stade de France on Friday. Les Bleus' fourth victory from five pool matches ensured they kept their lead in the northern group standings. England ran in 13 tries as they thrashed Japan 78-15 to close the gap to France to just one point. Ireland are on the same points total as England after recovering from a slow start to overwhelm Fiji 43-15. France face Argentina in the last round and will be favourites to take their place in the final on Sunday, 29 November, but England and Ireland will be hoping they slip up. The finals weekend takes place from 27-29 November, with all six matches at Allianz Stadium. Check out lower down this page who might play who - and when - in the play-off fixtures. Standings Autumn fixtures & results Friday, 6 November Ireland 42-12 Argentina Saturday, 7 November Italy 7-66 South Africa Scotland 21-43 New Zealand Wales 28-21 Japan France 54-17 Fiji Sunday, 8 November England 45-22 Australia Friday, 13 November France 21-19 South Africa Saturday, 14 November Italy 14-19 Argentina Wales 35-28 New Zealand England 78-15 Japan Ireland 43-15 Fiji Sunday, 15 November Scotland v Australia (15:10 GMT) Saturday, 21 November England v New Zealand (14:10 GMT) Scotland v Japan (14:10 GMT) Ireland v South Africa (16:40 GMT) Italy v Fiji (16:40 GMT) France v Argentina (20:10 GMT) Wales v Australia (20:10 GMT) What is the Nations Championship? The Nations Championship pits the northern hemisphere teams who compete in the Six Nations - England, Ireland, Scotland, Wales, France and Italy - against southern hemisphere giants South Africa, New Zealand, Australia and Argentina, plus invited sides Fiji and Japan. All teams will play each of the six in the opposing hemisphere once, with three rounds of fixtures staged in July and another three in November. Their results will rank the teams within their own hemisphere, from one to six. On the final weekend in November, there is a three-day play-off event staged at Allianz Stadium in Twickenham. The sixth-placed team in the northern hemisphere plays off against the equivalent in the southern hemisphere standings and so on, culminating in the two top-ranked sides taking each other on. The winner of that final match is crowned the inaugural Nations Championship winner. There is also a parallel, Ryder-Cup style hemisphere title. The winner of each of the matches on the play-offs weekend will earn one point for their hemisphere, except for the contest between the two top-ranked teams which delivers two. The first hemisphere to earn four points over the weekend will be crowned winners. item.title: Mirra Andreeva sees off Jessica Pegula to reach WTA Finals showpiece
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Russian tennis player Mirra Andreeva celebrates a point against Poland's Iga Swiatek during their women's singles quarterfinal match of the Stuttgart Open tennis tournament. (is associated with: «Mirra Andreeva sees off Jessica Pegula to reach WTA Finals showpiece») Marijan Murat/dpa Mirra Andreeva stormed into the final of the WTA Finals for the first time and in the process got the last laugh over Jessica Pegula. Andreeva produced a near immaculate display in Indian Wells to win 6-3, 6-4 in 85 minutes and claim a semblance of revenge against her American rival. Pegula made headlines before the end-of-season tournament started when she made disparaging comments about Andreeva’s mentality to her coach during a training session, which were picked up on a livestream that the world number five had not been aware of. The ‘hot mic’ moment failed to stop Pegula qualifying into the semi-finals, but she had no answer to Andreeva after a shaky start. A double fault by Andreeva gifted Pegula an early break before she showed supreme mental strength to remain calm and break back with a fine crosscourt winner, and a wonderful backhand winner sealed another to move 5-3 up to help clinch set one. The second set followed a similar pattern with Pegula able to go a break up for a 3-1 lead but unable to press home her advantage, and Andreeva won five out of the final six games to reach Sunday’s showpiece without dropping a set.

item.title: Best content of the week: Interview with Brad Holmes in Munich
item.description: It’s official. The Detroit Lions and their fans have taken over Munich, Germany, ahead of their Week 10 matchup against the New England Patriots. Lions legends like Barry Sanders and Calvin Johnson are tapping kegs along with principal owner and chairwoman Sheila Hamp. Big Sean is in town. Lions star wide receiver Jameson Williams is taking his love for McDonald’s across the pond. In the middle of the Honolulu blue wave, we are also getting some excellent content. From Jeremy Reisman singing, “ Hail to the Victors ,” with other Lions fans, to the exclusive interview Colton Pouncy of The Athletic landed with Lions general manager Brad Holmes. You’ll want to read the interview with Holmes, especially since it covers his mindset on the NFL trade deadline and his message to fans who think he is being complacent. “Complacency doesn’t exist in our process,” Holmes said. “We made the moves that we made because we got a player that we liked on a deal. Whatever we did, it’s not indicative of our work ethic or complacency or our process. The trade deadline happens to have a title on it, but it’s really not any other different week besides — you might get an uptick in phone calls, but we’re calling and working the phones all year. Like, we’re doing this stuff in August and September, October. We’re doing this all the time, year-round. So, there’s no complacency. Nobody’s in position to be complacent. You’ve probably heard me say multiple times, I never think it’s enough. No matter how talented our roster gets, it’s never enough. And once you think it’s enough, that’s when you’ll get beat. So, there’s never complacency. You can read the entire article from Pouncy right here . And now, on to the rest of the best Lions content from this week. Lions special teams coordinator Dave Fipp with an awesome tribute for veterans everywhere on the heels of him being named the Salute to Service nominee in Detroit. Dave Fipp, the Lions’ Salute to Service nominee, with a touching tribute to all who serve — and to mothers everywhere — for their selflessness. “It's a quality that we don’t emphasize in society today.” Said he’s “embarrassed” to even be mentioned in the same breath as them. pic.twitter.com/vNCX3bHSDV — Will Burchfield (@burchie_kid) November 12, 2026 We also have another story from Will Burchfield of 97.1 on Lions left guard Christian Mahogany taking full responsibility for what happened prior to the Week 9 win in Miami. Christian Mahogany: "It sucks what happened, but I have to grow up and stop breaking team rules. I let my teammates down, I let my organization down and it won’t ever happen again." He apologized to the team this morn and is slated to start in Germany: https://t.co/mo9zxdklP8 — Will Burchfield (@burchie_kid) November 11, 2026 Kegatron is really good. Kegatron's on the loose in Munich pic.twitter.com/PA9qv7WE94 — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 13, 2026 Richard Silva of The Detroit News wrote a great piece on Lions star receiver Amon-Ra St. Bro
