item.title: 3 Takeaways from the Atlanta Hawks Ugly Loss to the Chicago Bulls
item.description: ; Chicago Bulls forward Matas Buzelis (14) and Atlanta Hawks guard CJ McCollum (3) chase the ball during the second half at United Center. Photo Credit: Mandatory Credit: Matt Marton-Imagn Images | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Daniel Benjamin, Editor The Atlanta Hawks suffered an ugly loss to the Chicago Bulls on Friday night in an Emirates NBA Cup game, dropping them to 7-6 on the year. The Bulls entered the game on a downward spiral after starting the season 1-9. Even worse for Chicago, Caleb Wilson, their fourth overall draft pick , was ruled out for four to six weeks with a hand fracture. Combine the 1-9 start with the loss of their star rookie, and it appears the Bulls’ season is continuing to go downhill. Meanwhile, the Hawks came into the game as heavy favorites, all things considered. However, the game is played on the floor, not on spreadsheets. A lot went wrong for Atlanta last night. The Hawks Couldn’t Defend the Three-Point Line The Bulls are the worst three-point shooting team in the NBA. Before their game against the Hawks, Chicago was below 30% from three. That didn’t stop them from shooting 40% from beyond the arc with 20 made threes on the night. Patrick Williams, in particular, entered the game with one made three on the season. He scored 13 points and made four three-pointers, both season-high marks. The three-point barrage helped the Bulls build an 18-point lead in the second quarter. To Atlanta’s credit, they fought back and cut into the deficit, but their inability to defend the three-point line dug them into that hole. Over half of Chicago’s made threes came in the first half. They knocked down 11 threes over the first 24 minutes, while the Hawks made eight total all game. The Bulls hit 20 threes and still put up only a 107.8 offensive rating tonight against Atlanta. On the other end, the Bulls came into the night with the worst defensive rating in the NBA this season. In short, offense was the (MUCH) bigger issue for the Hawks than the defense. — Brad Rowland (@BTRowland) November 14, 2026 Lack Of Playmaking Crushed the Hawks’ Offense Jalen Johnson , Dyson Daniels and Kingston Flemings are undoubtedly the three best playmakers on Atlanta’s roster. The offense runs smoother with them on the floor. In lineups where all three of them are on the bench, the Hawks have a -26.1 net rating. When Daniels, in particular, is out of the lineup, Atlanta has a -10.5 net rating, compared to +7.7 when he’s on the floor. The Hawks have run a four-man group featuring Nickeil Alexander-Walker , Lu Dort , CJ McCollum and Aaron Wiggins , none of whom are point guards or playmakers. Against the Bulls, that lineup generated a -33.3 net rating in 11 minutes. Over the season, that group has a -26.7 net rating in 36 minutes played. It’s clear that Atlanta struggles to run offense without one of their primary playmakers on the floor, and the game against Chicago was no different. Over the season, Daniels is only averaging 30.8 minutes per game. In

Photo Credit: Mandatory Credit: Matt Marton-Imagn Images | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Daniel Benjamin, Editor The Atlanta Hawks suffered an ugly loss to the Chicago Bulls on Friday night in an Emirates NBA Cup game, dropping them to 7-6 on the year. The Bulls entered the game on a downward spiral after starting the season 1-9. Combine the 1-9 start with the loss of their star rookie, and it appears the Bulls’ season is continuing to go downhill. Meanwhile, the Hawks came into the game as heavy favorites, all things considered. However, the game is played on the floor, not on spreadsheets. A lot went wrong for Atlanta last night. The Hawks Couldn’t Defend the Three-Point Line The Bulls are the worst three-point shooting team in the NBA. Before their game against the Hawks, Chicago was below 30% from three. That didn’t stop them from shooting 40% from beyond the arc with 20 made threes on the night. Patrick Williams, in particular, entered the game with one made three on the season. He scored 13 points and made four three-pointers, both season-high marks. The three-point barrage helped the Bulls build an 18-point lead in the second quarter. To Atlanta’s credit, they fought back and cut into the deficit, but their inability to defend the three-point line dug them into that hole. Over half of Chicago’s made threes came in the first half. They knocked down 11 threes over the first 24 minutes, while the Hawks made eight total all game. The Bulls hit 20 threes and still put up only a 107.8 offensive rating tonight against Atlanta. On the other end, the Bulls came into the night with the worst defensive rating in the NBA this season. In short, offense was the (MUCH) bigger issue for the Hawks than the defense. — Brad Rowland (@BTRowland) November 14, 2026 Lack Of Playmaking Crushed the Hawks’ Offense Jalen Johnson , Dyson Daniels and Kingston Flemings are undoubtedly the three best playmakers on Atlanta’s roster. The offense runs smoother with them on the floor. In lineups where all three of them are on the bench, the Hawks have a -26.1 net rating. When Daniels, in particular, is out of the lineup, Atlanta has a -10.5 net rating, compared to +7.7 when he’s on the floor. The Hawks have run a four-man group featuring Nickeil Alexander-Walker , Lu Dort , CJ McCollum and Aaron Wiggins , none of whom are point guards or playmakers. Against the Bulls, that lineup generated a -33.3 net rating in 11 minutes. Over the season, that group has a -26.7 net rating in 36 minutes played. It’s clear that Atlanta struggles to run offense without one of their primary playmakers on the floor, and the game against Chicago was no different. Over the season, Daniels is only averaging 30.8 minutes per game. In the previous two seasons with the Hawks, he averaged over 33 minutes per game. There’s an argument to be made that he should get more playing time because of his impact on both ends of the floor. Atlanta’s offense is better with him on the floor. Running Wiggins in lineups with Alexander-Walker and McCollum doesn’t work, as evidenced by a -17.9 net rating over 48 minutes. Replace Wiggins with Daniels, and that four-man lineup jumps to a +15.6 net rating in 44 minutes. The Hawks Falter in Overtime Chicago Bulls forward Matas Buzelis (14) signals after he scored a basket during overtime against the Atlanta Hawks at United Center. Photo Credit: Matt Marton, Imagn Images via Reuters Connect Atlanta made a comeback and had a chance at a game-winner in regulation. However, after Aaron Wiggins fumbled the ball out of bounds, the Hawks and Bulls played in their first overtime games of the season. Things started off well when Atlanta scored first in overtime. Chicago took control of the game after that as Norman Powell continued his masterful performance. Powell finished the game with 33 points on 76.2% true shooting. Part of that was the nine points he scored in overtime, on three field goals and three free throws. The Hawks failed to contain him and paid the price. In group play, Atlanta sits at 1-1 and is in third place in the NBA Cup standings. Norman Powell with the clutch OT and-1! @CHSN__ | @npowell2404 pic.twitter.com/OOw1npaoAM — Chicago Bulls (@chicagobulls) November 14, 2026 The Last Word On Hawks Ugly Loss The Hawks will play another bottom-feeder, the Milwaukee Bucks, on Sunday. Kingston Flemings came into the Bulls game with a back injury. Although he was available, he reaggravated the injury and only played in 17 minutes. His availability for the Bucks game is uncertain. Despite the back-to-back losses, Atlanta still remains within 3.5 games of the first seed. The schedule will tighten up, however, as the Hawks play three of their next six games against teams with eight or more wins. item.title: Sabalenka apologises & says viral comment 'not directed at Svitolina'
item.description: Aryna Sabalenka will be replaced as world number two by Mirra Andreeva on Monday [Getty Images] Aryna Sabalenka has apologised and denied claims that she insulted opponent Elina Svitolina after a viral clip showed her swearing during her WTA Finals defeat by the Ukrainian. A video of world number two Sabalenka angrily gesturing and swearing in Russian during her 6-3 3-6 6-1 defeat by Ukraine's Svitolina was posted on social media on Saturday. Some commentators interpreted Belarusian Sabalenka's comments as an insult towards Svitolina or Ukrainians in general. Sabalenka later wrote on social media that "my comment was not directed at Elina" but she lost her temper because of the behaviour of some fans. "I was frustrated with a small group of spectators who were aggressively cheering my mistakes, and I reacted emotionally in the moment," the 28-year-old wrote. "That said, I should have handled my frustration differently, and I apologise to anyone offended." Sabalenka said Svitolina had played a great match, adding that she wished her "all the best for the rest of the tournament". Ukrainian players have a long-standing policy of not shaking hands with Russian or Belarusian players because of the ongoing invasion of their country. They also do not take pre-match photographs with each other. Nerveless Andreeva reaches WTA Finals showpiece Sabalenka's season ended by Svitolina at WTA Finals Live scores, results and order of play

item.title: Nerveless Andreeva reaches WTA Finals showpiece
item.description: Mirra Andreeva won the Indian Wells title - part of the WTA Tour - last year [Getty Images] Mirra Andreeva says she surprised herself with her nerveless performance after beating Jessica Pegula to become the youngest player for 22 years to reach the WTA Finals showpiece. French Open champion Andreeva came back from a break down in both sets to win 6-3 6-4 in Indian Wells, California. The 19-year-old Russian is the youngest finalist at the season-ending event since Maria Sharapova, who was 17 when she won the title in 2004. Victory over American Pegula ensures Andreeva will finish the year as world number two. "I did not feel one bit of pressure today, I don't know why," Andreeva told Sky Sports. "Usually I feel like on these important points or when I have to close out the match or the set I get so tight. "But for some reason today I was just playing. I was just not thinking about anything, just trying to enjoy." Tournament debutant Andreeva has yet to drop a set and has not lost more than four games in any of her eight sets. The 18 games she has lost is the fewest for a finalist at the WTA Finals since the round-robin format was introduced in 2003. Under the guidance of coach Conchita Martinez, Andreeva has developed her serve into a real weapon. She won 77% of points behind her first serve and hit 17 winners to outmuscle Pegula. Andreeva also showed impressive composure, remaining unfazed despite going an early break down in both sets against the home favourite. She will play Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova or 2019 WTA Finals champion Elina Svitolina in Sunday's final. Sabalenka apologises & says viral comment 'not directed at Svitolina' Sabalenka's season ended by Svitolina at WTA Finals
item.content:encoded: Mirra Andreeva won the Indian Wells title - part of the WTA Tour - last year [Getty Images] Mirra Andreeva says she surprised herself with her nerveless performance after beating Jessica Pegula to become the youngest player for 22 years to reach the WTA Finals showpiece. French Open champion Andreeva came back from a break down in both sets to win 6-3 6-4 in Indian Wells, California. The 19-year-old Russian is the youngest finalist at the season-ending event since Maria Sharapova, who was 17 when she won the title in 2004. Victory over American Pegula ensures Andreeva will finish the year as world number two. "I did not feel one bit of pressure today, I don't know why," Andreeva told Sky Sports. "Usually I feel like on these important points or when I have to close out the match or the set I get so tight. "But for some reason today I was just playing. I was just not thinking about anything, just trying to enjoy." Tournament debutant Andreeva has yet to drop a set and has not lost more than four games in any of her eight sets. The 18 games she has lost is the fewest for a finalist at the WTA Finals since the round-robin format was introduced in 2003. Under the guidance of coach Conchita Martinez, Andreeva has developed her serve into a real weapon. She won 77% of points behind her first serve and hit 17 winners to outmuscle Pegula. Andreeva also showed impressive composure, remaining unfazed despite going an early break down in both sets against the home favourite. She will play Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova or 2019 WTA Finals champion Elina Svitolina in Sunday's final. item.title: When Drake met Bastin: A chance family encounter at Arsenal
item.description: When Drake met Bastin: A chance family encounter at Arsenal On what some might call a divinely orchestrated day, I had what remains my most surreal experience at an Arsenal game. I can remember it as clear as daylight. It was 14 March 2019, and Arsenal were due to play French side Rennes in the Europa League round of 16. They would eventually win 3-0 to reach the quarter-finals. A chance encounter at the Emirates I was standing with an old school and college friend among hundreds of fans in the concourse, waiting to go and sit down for the match. I couldn’t help but look at the Arsenal hat-trick heroes board, which showed every single hat-trick my great-grandad, 1930s Gunners legend Ted Drake, scored. Something inside me told me to tell the slightly older guy with ginger hair and black glasses next to me who my great-grandfather was. Well, by pure coincidence, he told me he was the great-nephew or great-great-nephew of Cliff Bastin, Arsenal’s all-time top goalscorer from the 1930s through to the late 1990s , when Ian Wright broke his record of 178 goals. I asked if he had ever met Cliff. He said he hadn’t, which was ironic considering I’d never met Ted either. My school friend looked stunned. What are the chances, eh? Out of 60,000 people, I was apparently speaking to someone with Arsenal in their DNA too! Well, that’s a moment I’ll never forget, for sure! Highbury 1935. (L-R): Wilf Copping, Cliff Bastin, Eddie Hapgood, Ted Drake, George Male. (Photo by J.A Hampton/Topical Press Agency/Getty Images) Two families with Arsenal in their DNA Drake set the English top-flight record for the most goals scored in a game when he hit seven away to Aston Villa on 14 December 1935. From his arrival in 1934 through to 1939, he was Arsenal’s top scorer every season, scoring 44 goals in the 1934/35 campaign, a tally no Arsenal striker has beaten. I was 16 at the time, and I told Cliff’s relative how much I respected what both players had achieved for the club and that I couldn’t believe the odds. I texted a family member moments later! During the 2022/23 season, while I was involved in the Emirates Stadium banner redesign project, I did meet the daughter and grandson of Eddie Hapgood, Arsenal’s 1930s captain and legendary defender. But that experience in the concourse was certainly more surreal in some ways! Liam Harding Have you ever had a chance encounter at an Arsenal match that’s stayed with you? item.content:encoded: PISCATAWAY, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 14: Luke Lindenmeyer #8 of the Nebraska Cornhuskers scores a touchdown against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights in the first quarter at SHI Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Piscataway, New Jersey. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images The mythical overlords of college football finally teed one up for the Huskers, and they in turn took care of business emphatically enough to perhaps allow a day or two of grace and maybe even enjoyment. Of course, the grumblers will begin loading their chambers for Ohio State and Iowa weekends quickly enough. And if we’re honest, there were still moments of jaws dropping and muttered curses. Pre-snap penalties in each of the first two drives. Glenn Thomas not being heard because his mouth wasn’t close enough to the headset mic. A timeout burned early. A dropped TD pass. And a couple of questionable 4th down calls on the coaching end. Just wanted to get that out of the way early as the players seemed to clean up their act early. The offense blazed through Rutgers for a pair of 90+ yard drives as well as 237 yards rushing, 103 by true freshman Jamal Rule who got a lot of them physically – which could be witnessed by Rutgers defenders on the field. The defense exceeded expectations with a donut on the board as they held Rutgers to 143 total yards. Not much was expected – the Scarlet Knights started their 3rd string QB and had to return to their gametime-decision backup signal caller after QB3 was knocked out of the game. Best player and WR KJ Duff had season-ending surgery earlier in the week. With these circumstances, the Blackshirts were able to focus on shutting down the running game, and for the most part, they did. They also came up with picks the two times Rutgers threatened. Thank you Caleb Benning and Jeremiah Charles. The final was 31-0. Along with Rule, there was Anthony Colandrea running things smoothly by throwing for 188 yards and a pair of scores while rushing for 68 and another on the ground. Carter Nelson, whose name keeps popping up more and more, had a pair of grabs as well as a 40-yarder which set up another ( Correction: only one TD grab, not two ) . On the defensive side, it was Vincent Shavers covering for the injured Own Chambliss with 10 tackles. The game didn’t begin lights out. The Huskers thought they had a 3 & out, but Rutgers went and made a 4th & 1 from their own 34. They picked up a few more yards before burying Nebraska on their 5 when Jacory Barney opted to fair catch one there. No problem as – check that, a familiar problem when they took a false start on their second play. But Nebraska began marching ripping off chunks of 15 and 18 yards by Rule and Colandrea respectively. Colandrea then hit Barney for a 38-yard TD pass…except the review showed he dropped it. In this case, no problem, the Huskers kept driving and Colandrea found Luke Lindenmeyer for 15 yards on a 3rd & 9, and he rumbled in for the game’s opening score. The Huskers’ second drive was fouled with a pair of pre-snap penalties after beginning when Barney fielded a second straight punt on the 5 and returned it only to the 8. The third one also started deep in their own territory when a Rutgers punt found its way out of bounds at the 10 this time. However, they were on the move, again mostly by ground, until Colandrea found Carter Nelson behind the Rutgers secondary and when he was done running, the Huskers were 40 yards downfield on the Rutgers 6. Colandrea hopped in from there for the 14-0 lead and it was becoming pretty obvious this was a mismatch. The Huskers began the 3rd quarter with a short march which found them on their 45 with a 4th and 1. “You should be able to get 1 the way you’ve been running it,” was true enough, but so was the fact it also seemed like a nice time to perhaps flip the field position battle after three straight 90+ yard drives in front of them – especially against an offense which had only managed 65 yards of 1st half offense. Things seemed a little shaky when the Knights moved to the Husker 24. Uh oh? Nope, thanks to Benning who made his pick and return. The Huskers took advantage of their first short field to roll in with Mekhi Nelson finishing things off with runs of 11 and 10 yards to go up 21-0. In between, a targeting review, after Nelson took the crown of Tariq Hayer’s helmet in his earhole, actually went Nebraska’s way! This may have been the first time a Cornhusker had actually had such a call applied to the opposition since 1897 or so. Hayer was helped off the field after the infraction, and while a lesser person might make a point of joyous karma rearing its head – but leading with its shoulder, not its helmet – I sincerely hope the injury was not serious. No way of knowing, since his ejection plus bar noise left me unable to know for sure. On their next possession, the Huskers again found themselves with a 4th down near midfield, this time at their 48. The call? Fake punt with Carter Nelson coming up short on a throw which…let’s be nice and just say it was not so great. And again, the call seemed the epitome of unnecessary – 21-point lead, lousy Rutgers offense, chance to drop them in the chum bucket with a good punt. Sigh. But it also resulted in no damage as the Blackshirts sent them packing with a 4 & out and a turnover on downs. It only took Nebraska five plays for Colandrea to hit Carter Nelson with a 13-yard TD pass for a 28-0 lead. They weren’t quite done, however. The next drive brought them far enough upfield to trot John Hohl out for a 41-yard field goal attempt. When it split the uprights, the Tiger Tom’s crowd let loose with its biggest cheer of the day. Judging by some of the laughs, a few of those cheers may have been tinged with sarcasm. Well, Notre Dame fans still believe their players carried Rudy off the field as genuine respect, despite Joe Montana saying for years they were all giggling at the joke. If they can think of that litter box of fiction as truth, then I choose to believe everyone was genuinely happy for Hohl. I know I was excited. 🌽🏈🙅🏻‍♂️ OMG, we love you John Hohl. It’s a field goal, dammit, A FIELD GOAL!!! pic.twitter.com/l3QrwFgUg7 — Corn Nation (@CornNation) November 14, 2026 Hohl’s boot gave the game its final score of 31-0 and brought on the backups. When the gun sounded, two things happened: 1) The Huskers became bowl-eligible for the 3rd straight season, the first time such a thing has happened since the Bo Pelini Era. I’m not saying that to calm those who have become so enraged this season; just pointing out a fact. 2) The Huskers notched their first shutout since the 2009 Holiday Bowl when Ndamukong Suh and the rest of the Blackshirts took out their “one more second” rage on Nick Foles and the Arizona Wildcats by the score of 33-0. This was obviously prior to their joining the Big 10 in 2011. Their last shutout in any conference play actually occurred back in 2003, a 28-0 blanking of Iowa State. As for the current Huskers, while they can’t erase the losing streak, their final games offer a chance at some redemption. Ohio State is certainly ripe for the picking after Julian Sayen went down for the season. And Iowa’s just doing Iowa things, not looking too scary very often, just hanging around and waiting for opponents to goof up and stealing that Amazon package off the porch when they look the other way. It’s a low-ceiling, high-floor approach which seems to satisfy their pasty denizens and teams. Nebraska, despite the rough start today, brought the penalties down, minus 25 yards of them back-to-back in garbage time. But if they can’t clean those up more – plus a few more areas – that Hawkeye approach certainly seems like a good way to win their fourth straight against the Huskers as well as 11 of the last 12 on Black Friday. But first, the Buckeyes. And a final chance to take down a big program finding themselves in a down year. Can they finally grab it? Stay tuned. x

item.title: Soroka Fits Houston’s Needs, Skubal A Fit for Everyone
item.description: Aug 22, 2026; Phoenix, Arizona, USA; Arizona Diamondbacks pitcher Michael Soroka (34) throws against the Cincinnati Reds in the fourth inning at Chase Field. Mandatory Credit: Anna Carrington-Imagn Images The Houston Astros face a real problem at Daikin Park. The stadium is not kind to pitchers, especially those who struggle with right-handed hitters. In 2026, the park had a home run factor of 113, which is very high by Sports Illustrated’s standards . Right-handed batters hit even more homers there, with a factor of 117. The left-field porch is only 315 feet, making it easy for power hitters to clear the fence. Houston pitchers allowed 204 home runs in 2026, the second-highest total in the majors, trailing only the Athletics. That makes limiting home runs a significant priority for the Astros this offseason. The team needs a pitcher who can keep the ball on the ground or in the strike zone. Michael Soroka from the Arizona Diamondbacks looks like a smart fit for this specific need. Limiting home runs is something he has proven possible without depending on strikeouts for survival. Why Soroka Makes Sense for Houston Soroka offers a balance that other options lack . The Astros looked at Dustin May and Casey Mize, but both have shown vulnerability to home runs. Last year Clay Holmes had a 20.7% home run rate on pulled balls, which rose to 29.4% this season. May improved his numbers, but Mize’s decline is worrying, with his expected FIP rising from 6.60 to 8.45. Soroka is different. He had his best season back in 2019 with the Atlanta Braves. He posted a 2.68 ERA and a 3.85 xFIP across 29 starts. That year, he threw 174 and two-thirds innings and recorded 4.0 fWAR. He was a revelation then, and his recent recovery from injury suggests he could be that pitcher again. He does not need to strike everyone out to be effective. The Mets Need Bigger Stars While Houston might sign Soroka, the New York Mets should not settle for a mid-tier addition. The Mets are in a different league when it comes to spending. They have the cash to make a record-setting deal for a true ace like Tarik Skubal. Joel Reuter of Bleacher Report placed the Mets at the top of the list for Skubal. He noted that the front office is not afraid to spend money to win. Reuter wrote, “In terms of sheer spending power and roster need, there is no more obvious landing spot for Skubal on a record-setting, long-term deal.” The Mets have already spent big on Max Scherzer and Justin Verlander in the past. They need to keep that momentum going this winter. Skubal, a 29-year-old left-hander, posted a combined 2.72 ERA with 186 strikeouts in 158⅔ innings between Detroit and Los Angeles in 2026. After being traded to the Dodgers in August, he recorded a 2.61 ERA and 70 strikeouts in 62 innings. Skubal was traded from the Detroit Tigers in August 2026. Detroit selected Skubal in the ninth round of the 2018 MLB Draft with the 255th overall pick. His most productive year was 2025, when he had a 2.21 ERA

The Mets need to show him a clear path to the World Series.

item.title: Comeback kid Joseph thrills as England eye All Blacks
item.description: Eddie Jones aired a complaint about Twickenham's in-stadium experience when he appeared on BBC Radio 5 Live this week. "Being a spectator and being told when to make noise is a bit funny," said the Japan boss, objecting to a big-screen request for an increase in volume. Jones sat stony-faced in the coaching box as the message appeared again in the midst of his team's 78-15 thrashing at England's hands on Saturday. There was little for him to enjoy on his return to Twickenham, where he was head coach for seven years. But, for the rest of a capacity crowd, it was a fun one. With junior tickets on sale at £15, there was a different atmosphere from usual. The decibels were higher, the demographic was younger, the spirits a little lighter. And England brought plenty of entertainment to the party. Thirteen tries in total, with Will Joseph's five putting him in the centre of the chorus line. The 24-year-old won his only previous England cap under Jones. Back in the summer of 2022, he was a teenage apprentice taken on tour to Australia and thrust into the second Test as a last-minute replacement. His promise has taken some time to be fulfilled. He struggled for game time and fitness at Harlequins after London Irish's bankruptcy forced him to move on from his boyhood club. An auto-immune condition that cost him the hearing in his left ear was one setback at the Stoop. But, as part of a rat pack of exciting young English-qualified backs at Gloucester this season, he has been superb: a swerving, offloading, game-breaking threat either on the wing or in midfield. England deployed him out wide, to bring some of the razzle-dazzle that they lost as Immanuel Feyi-Waboso limped out of their autumn campaign. Reports from Pennyhill Park during the week had suggested Joseph was doing a fine job of replicating Feyi-Waboso's explosive elusiveness. He certainly did on Twickenham's main stage, finishing chances with the same pace and power. "He is pretty similar to Immanuel Feyi-Waboso in the way he plays his game," said former England wing Chris Ashton on BBC Radio 5 Live. "He is just so fast. He doesn't look too fast in the first two steps and then he is just gone. He gets away from people." Joseph's cartwheeling plant of the ball over the line for his fourth summed up his exuberance. In the aftermath of that score, Japan flanker Ben Gunter put a consoling arm around full-back Kazuma Ueda, who had been comprehensively burned in a race to the corner. Japan couldn't get near Joseph, whose first try came after just 60 seconds and his hat-trick score in the 19th minute. "It has been a challenging four years, but I have enjoyed the journey to get back here and I am happy all that hard work I have put in has paid off," he said. "I have had a taste for it now and I can't wait to do it again." Nations Championship: Fixtures and standings Rugby Union Weekly: The greatest win in Welsh rugby history? "He is pretty similar to Immanuel Feyi-Waboso in the way he plays his game," said former England wing Chris Ashton on BBC Radio 5 Live. "He is just so fast. He doesn't look too fast in the first two steps and then he is just gone. He gets away from people." Joseph's cartwheeling plant of the ball over the line for his fourth summed up his exuberance. In the aftermath of that score, Japan flanker Ben Gunter put a consoling arm around full-back Kazuma Ueda, who had been comprehensively burned in a race to the corner. "I have had a taste for it now and I can't wait to do it again." Nations Championship: Fixtures and standings Rugby Union Weekly: The greatest win in Welsh rugby history? Will five-try Joseph face All Blacks? We have been here before though. There was another teenage apprentice taken on that tour of Australia alongside Joseph. Henry Arundell was Joseph's Irish team-mate. His impact on the trip was greater, scoring a try in the first Test and winning his second and third caps in the series. The following year, while Joseph returned to the club scene, Arundell made his first England start in the Six Nations. He earned a place in the Rugby World Cup squad and, in a foregone conclusion of a pool match, cantered in for five tries against Chile in Lille. Arundell was electric against limited opposition. He has yet to convince in sterner Tests. Joseph still has those to come. A shade slower, but a smidge smarter, he may be better suited to the Test scene. New Zealand next Saturday, stung by defeat by Wales, would definitely be a step up if Steve Borthwick decides to find out. Arundell and Joseph on England duty together in 2022 [Getty Images] There was plenty elsewhere to please the head coach. George Martin was at his abrasive best. The Saracens second row led England's carry and tackle standings in the comeback performance we have been waiting for since his 14-month injury lay-off ended in May. Ellis Genge was snorting fire and bruising ribs and Maro Itoje's rejuvenation after a summer off continues. In the backline, Max Ojomoh was too clever and quick for the Japanese midfield, spotting space either for himself or others. Henry Pollock, the other point of interest in a much-changed line-up, found it harder to get into the game with ball in hand, but did the dirty work in defence and at the breakdown that some have questioned. Borthwick will be waiting nervously on news from his medical room this week, with Ollie Chessum, Seb Atkinson and George Furbank hoping to return in time for the All Blacks. But a fourth win in a row, after five successive defeats, has further buoyed up his regime. "The team is really starting to play well," he told BBC 5 Live. "The speed and positioning in attack was very good which gave us options to be able to move the ball. "There was intent to play fast, with all the strengths of English rugby. We've got some really great attacking talent and I think we are seeing that. "The balance of pass-kick decisions was really good. Ultimately I think one of the main things is the supporters really enjoyed it. The atmosphere was excellent." Even Jones, who had Borthwick as an assistant during a previous stint with Japan and his time with England, managed a smile by the end. "It kills me that Will Joseph, I gave him his first cap, he scores five tries against me. Now that's not being very loyal, is it?," he joked. "He's a great kid. He always was going to be a good player." England will hope he might turn out even better than that. 'An almost perfect day' - Joseph scores five tries as ruthless England thrash Japan

item.title: Austin Championship: Trace Crowe grabs 54-hole lead late
item.description: Trace Crowe birdied his final two holes Saturday to get to 14 under and separate himself from three other players through 54 holes of the inaugural Austin Championship . Chad Ramey, Erik van Rooyen and Sami Valimaki all could have shared the lead heading into Sunday's final round at Fazio Canyons Golf Course if Crowe had faltered down the stretch. But the 30-year-old Crowe, who is seeking his first win on Tour this week in Texas, birdied the par-3 17th and followed it up with another circle at No. 18 as part of the final grouping on the course. Heavy winds began to impact players still on their back nines Saturday afternoon, and Crowe was no exception. After setting the course record on Thursday with an opening-round 62, Crowe bogeyed the first two holes on his back nine on Moving Day. Another square at the par-4 16th put his chances in doubt but the run of birdies at the end of his round vaulted him ahead for the solo lead. Americans Ben Kohles and Max Greyserman are two back of Crowe's lead, while eight players sit T-7 at 11 under. Ramey had the clubhouse lead for more than an hour. He got there by limiting mistakes — the 34-year-old Mississippi State alum has posted just three bogeys, one in each round. Saturday's error came at the par-3 17th, the same hole Crowe birdied from an hour later. "On a week like this to kind of finally get some good results and be in a good position going into Sunday, it's great to see," said Ramey, who entered the week No. 136 in the FedExCup Fall standings and has moved up to a projected No. 68. That would give Ramey a card for 2027, despite not having a top 10 finish in his first 26 starts. Valimaki, who won for the first time at the RSM Classic last November , moved into the co-leader position with a 3-under 69. He opened the inaugural tournament 68-66 after making his first PGA Tour start since July at last week's WWT Championship. "It was good to take some time off, it's actually been a long time since I felt like I could enjoy the golf course and I feel like that's the biggest key for me," said Valimaki, who battled a right wrist injury and also received stiches in his left hand. The Finnish player was No. 172 entering the week but has crept up to No. 129 with 18 holes left. The top 100 players earn their cards , while players inside the top 125 earn conditional status for the 2027 season. Van Rooyen was more up and down with his 69 on Saturday. He bogeyed the 215-yard, par-3 eighth hole and followed that up with a double at the turn. A bogey at the 17th looked like it could sink his chances at the co-lead, but he answered by circling the par-5 18th. "Compared to the first two days, it's much trickier," said the South African, who has moved from No. 140 in the fall standings up to No. 108 with his play in Austin. "Wind was difficult. I thought some of the pins were really tricky, and it was cold so the ball's just not going as far." The final round has been moved up due to inclement weather expected in the ar

item.title: Trevon Diggs among players being activated from practice squad for Seahawks-Raiders game
item.description: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Trevon Diggs among players being activated from practice squad for Seahawks-Raiders game appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Seattle Seahawks are elevating veteran cornerback Trevon Diggs and offensive tackle Bobby Hart from the practice squad ahead of their Week 10 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders . As the Seahawks (5-4) prepare to visit Fernando Mendoza and the Raiders (4-5) on Sunday at 1:05 p.m. PT on CBS, Diggs will have another opportunity to contribute to Seattle’s secondary. NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reported the roster moves Saturday via X, formerly known as Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “The #Seahawks elevated CB Trevon Diggs and OT Bobby Hart from the practice squad ahead of Sunday’s game against the #Raiders.” Diggs has appeared in four games for Seattle this season but has seen limited action. The 28-year-old has recorded one solo tackle and has yet to register an interception or pass breakup. PFF credits Diggs with 27 defensive snaps, including 24 in coverage . Trevon Diggs looking to make impact for Seahawks vs. Raiders Seattle signed Diggs in August after he spent his first six NFL seasons with the Dallas Cowboys before a brief stint with the Green Bay Packers. The former second-round pick has recorded 20 interceptions and 63 passes defensed across his NFL career. His 20 interceptions from 2020 through 2025 were tied for the second-most in the league over that span. Diggs’ best season came in 2021, when he earned first-team All-Pro honors after leading the NFL with 11 interceptions and returning two for touchdowns. The Seahawks have experienced an uneven start to their Super Bowl title defense but enter Sunday’s contest with an opportunity to build momentum. Seattle is coming off a 17-3 Week 9 victory over the Arizona Cardinals and will have its bye following the matchup with Las Vegas. Elevating Diggs gives Seattle another experienced option in the secondary before the team enters its Week 11 break. Related: Seahawks’ biggest mistake at 2026 NFL Trade Deadline after adding Quenton Nelson Related: Seahawks’ Charles Cross back at practice for first time since Week 7 with ankle injury

item.title: 'Painful' defeat for Republic of Ireland in Austria
item.description: Hallgrimsson's side sit third in Group B3 before their final game [Getty Images] Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson said their 1-0 defeat by Austria in their penultimate Nations League game was "painful". Substitute Sasa Kalajdzic poked home the winner in Linz, with the narrow victory ensuring Austria claimed top spot and automatic promotion to League A. Chiedozie Ogbene squandered a late chance to equalise and Hallgrimsson was frustrated that they left the Raiffeisen Arena empty-handed when they had chances to secure the win which would have kept their hopes of winning the group alive. "It was painful not to get anything from this match. I think we deserved at least a draw, but we needed the win for this game to count," he told RTE. "I think we had the chances, the openings and the positions to do that, but this was not our day in goal-scoring, so it is disappointing. "Everything that we asked the players to do, they did and I think they gave everything. "For that reason, we should be happy in a way but, obviously, we don't want to be building something, we want to win games." Austria seal top spot with win over Republic of Ireland 'It is all down to details' Saturday's defeat left Hallgrimsson's side third in Group B3, a point behind Kosovo, who they face in their final game in Dublin on Tuesday. Hallgrimsson was left to rue Republic of Ireland's inability to clear the corner that Kalajdzic scored from. "We actually did have a lot of chances from that second ball in the box but it kind of never fell for our players in a good position," he added. "They have a corner that they score from on the second or third touch. "That's the game at this level. You need to be switched on and focused every second of the game." Picking up a second win in the group against Kosovo would secure a second-place finish in the group which brings with it a promotion play-off and a move up to pot two for next month's Euro 2028 qualifying draw. The Irish fell to a 1-0 defeat in Pristina in September and Hallgrimsson needs his side to finish strongly at home and pick up a vital three points. "It was always that [Kosovo] game that was more important, but we were just so close to winning this one and being able to win the group but this is football at this level, it is all down to details."

item.title: Clark quarterback Rocky Orozco voted Express-News Athlete of the Week
item.description: Clark Cougars Rocky Orozco (9) throws a pass In the second half on Thursday, Oct.29, 2026 at Farris Stadium. Brandeis defeated Clark 56-29. (Ronald Cortes) Clark junior quarterback Rocky Orozco had a career day in the Cougars' regular-season finale. Orozco threw for 453 yards and five touchdowns on 25-of-40 passing as Clark put up a valiant effort but fell to Reagan in a 55-45 shootout to end the Cougars' season. Following up his stellar day throwing the football, he has now been voted the Express-News Athlete of the Week. He was named Offensive Player of the Week on Monday and beat out four fellow finalists in the Athlete of the Week poll. Medina Valley senior Slate Crisp, the Defensive Player of the Week, made 14 tackles, including two for losses, to headline a stellar defensive as the Panthers shut out South San 42-0 and secured an undefeated regular season and District 14-5A-I title. Alamo Heights junior running back William Bishop caught six passes for 105 yards and a touchdown in the Mules' 42-11 win over Liberty Hill Legacy Ranch, and he added 16 carries for 171 yards. Davenport senior Dakota Hart was named Volleyball Player of the Week. The senior libero combined for 45 digs in playoff sweeps against Marble Falls and La Vernia. She had 30 digs against the Bears to help the Wolves reach the state quarterfinals for the fourth straight season. New Braunfels senior Shaylie Schaefer combined for 28 kills and four blocks in a pair of playoff victories over Victoria West and Burbank to help the Unicorns advance to the state quarterfinals. She put up 20 kills against West. Subscribe There’s more to San Antonio with the Express-News. Subscribe today for just 25¢. item.title: SpaceX pulls off first-ever spaceship ‘catch’
item.description: Elon Musk’s SpaceX on Saturday carried out the first-ever recovery of a spaceship, pulling off a successful “catch” of its Starship vessel as it returned to its launch site after a day in orbit. The spaceship emerged from a cloudy sky after withstanding the extreme heat of re-entering the Earth’s atmosphere, and descended slowly over Starbase before slipping smoothly between mechanical “chopstick arms” above Launch Pad 2. The feat marked a milestone in the space industry’s decades-long pursuit of fully reusable rocket systems — a goal that can drastically reduce mission costs and make more frequent launches possible. “That was the Holy Grail of space flight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship and now, everything changes,” SpaceX spokesman Dan Huot said. Crowds gathered on the Gulf of Mexico beach near Starbase broke into cheers as the spaceship eased into its high-tech nest on the 15th test flight of the world’s biggest and most powerful rocket system. This time the Starship spacecraft that gives the rocket system its name orbited Earth 14 times and deployed 26 satellites for Musk’s Starlink satellite internet constellation during its 22-hour journey. Until now SpaceX had captured returning booster rockets three times. However, the “catch” of Starship was extraordinarily complex because the spaceship fell much faster and from a much higher altitude than boosters do. Clayton Swope, an aerospace expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, called the mission a “huge technical achievement and proves the whole idea of Starship as a fully reusable spaceship can work.” “Let’s see how quickly they can do it again,” he added. ‘Giant swoosh’ The vessel’s path home was carefully mapped out by engineers. “If you want to get back to the east coast of Texas, you have to fly over the entire continent to get back there. So inevitably, you’re flying over land and we spend a lot of time figuring out the safest way to do that,” senior SpaceX engineer Lars Blackmore said. Starship flew over sparsely inhabited desert areas, wove over towns and then carried out a “giant swoosh maneuver” in its final approach, looping around the cities of Texas’ Rio Grande Valley and approaching its landing site from the east. Some versions of Starship are designed to launch internet satellites and data centers into orbit, while other iterations will be made to ferry people to the Moon and Mars. US space agency NASA is expecting Starship to serve as a lunar lander on its Artemis mission. On Saturday, Administrator Jared Isaacman congratulated Musk and SpaceX. “It was almost magic… Making more believers by the day… one step closer to (the Moon),” he said on X. item.content:encoded: Elon Musk’s SpaceX on Saturday carried out the first-ever recovery of a spaceship, pulling off a successful “catch” of its Starship vessel as it returned to its launch site after a day in orbit. The spaceship emerged from a cloudy sky after withstanding the extreme heat of re-entering the Earth’s atmosphere, and descended slowly over Starbase before slipping smoothly between mechanical “chopstick arms” above Launch Pad 2. The feat marked a milestone in the space industry’s decades-long pursuit of fully reusable rocket systems — a goal that can drastically reduce mission costs and make more frequent launches possible. “That was the Holy Grail of space flight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship and now, everything changes,” SpaceX spokesman Dan Huot said. Crowds gathered on the Gulf of Mexico beach near Starbase broke into cheers as the spaceship eased into its high-tech nest on the 15th test flight of the world’s biggest and most powerful rocket system. This time the Starship spacecraft that gives the rocket system its name orbited Earth 14 times and deployed 26 satellites for Musk’s Starlink satellite internet constellation during its 22-hour journey. Until now SpaceX had captured returning booster rockets three times. However, the “catch” of Starship was extraordinarily complex because the spaceship fell much faster and from a much higher altitude than boosters do. Clayton Swope, an aerospace expert at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, called the mission a “huge technical achievement and proves the whole idea of Starship as a fully reusable spaceship can work.” “Let’s see how quickly they can do it again,” he added. ‘Giant swoosh’ The vessel’s path home was carefully mapped out by engineers. “If you want to get back to the east coast of Texas, you have to fly over the entire continent to get back there. So inevitably, you’re flying over land and we spend a lot of time figuring out the safest way to do that,” senior SpaceX engineer Lars Blackmore said. Starship flew over sparsely inhabited desert areas, wove over towns and then carried out a “giant swoosh maneuver” in its final approach, looping around the cities of Texas’ Rio Grande Valley and approaching its landing site from the east. Some versions of Starship are designed to launch internet satellites and data centers into orbit, while other iterations will be made to ferry people to the Moon and Mars. US space agency NASA is expecting Starship to serve as a lunar lander on its Artemis mission. On Saturday, Administrator Jared Isaacman congratulated Musk and SpaceX. “It was almost magic… Making more believers by the day… one step closer to (the Moon),” he said on X. Refueling challenge Musk, the world’s richest person, has already revolutionized the space sector with the partially reusable Falcon rockets, which regularly launch satellites and carry astronauts to the International Space Station. But the Starship project has been plagued by delays as SpaceX grapples with novel engineering challenges, including the unsolved problem of transferring fuel to the spaceship while in orbit — a requirement for any journey to the Moon or Mars. It will also need to further fine-tune the Super Heavy booster, which ran into a technical issue Friday on its descent, forcing a diversion to the Gulf of Mexico just off the launch site. It, too, was supposed to have been caught by the “chopstick arms.” The booster automatically self-destructed — a fireball erupting from the booster — before hitting the water. Following SpaceX’s high-profile stock market debut in June that raised about $85.7 billion, the company is investing heavily in production and launch capabilities. During a tour of its million-square-foot (93,000-square-meter) factory at Starbase on Friday, SpaceX officials told journalists it now has the capability to produce a spaceship every two weeks and a booster every four weeks. item.title: Denmark hammer Ronaldo-less Portugal 4-1 in Nations League match
item.description: Portugal were hammered 4-1 by Denmark on Saturday, an embarrassing Nations League defeat in their first match without Cristiano Ronaldo following the superstar forward’s retirement from international football. Rasmus Hojlund starred with a superb brace as Denmark moved into second place in Group A4 and closed in on a spot in the quarter-finals with a brilliant display in Braga. The Danes are on nine points from five fixtures, three behind Portugal who were already sure of qualification for the last eight having won all four of their previous group fixtures. A draw against third-placed Norway on Tuesday, 3-1 winners over Wales earlier, will see Denmark through. Ahead of kick-off Portugal paid tribute to Ronaldo, who announced his exit from the international game last week, with the team and mascots walking out wearing Ronaldo’s number seven and his name on their jerseys. Fans held up a huge banner which read “Thank you captain” as the teams entered the field, while applause rolled around the stadium once the match clock hit seven. Ronaldo made his debut for Portugal in 2003 and went on to establish world records for goals and appearances in international football, netting 146 times in 234 matches. The highlight of his international career was winning Euro 2016, but it ended badly when the 41-year-old fell out with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus over not being selected for a Nations League fixture in September. That row led to the five-time Ballon d’Or winner being handed a 30-day suspension by the Portuguese football federation and his subsequent retirement, and Portugal looked liked they needed prime Ronaldo in a dismal display. Denmark were the better team from the first minute and it was no surprise when the away team went in at the break thanks to Pierre-Emile’s Hojbjerg’s spot-kick in the 43rd minute. Hojlund lashed home a brilliant volley four minutes after the restart and seven minutes later left the home crowd shellshocked with a strike of which Ronaldo would have been proud, the Napoli striker skipping past Ruben Dias before crashing home a powerful shot from the edge of the area. Boos and whistles began to ring out at the Estadio Municipal when Joachim Andersen headed in the fourth, and Bernardo Silva’s late consolation effort barely dampened the discontent. Antonio Nusa opened the scoring for Norway just before the hour mark in Oslo with a fine low strike before Andreas Schjelderup tapped home a perfect low cross from Erling Haaland, who rounded off the scoring from the penalty spot two minutes from time. Wales briefly had hope of getting a result when David Brook’s chipped finish halved the deficit in the 79th minute, but Craig Bellamy’s team will finish bottom of the group and risk being relegated to League B. item.title: [VIDEO] ‘We’re The Only Party With 13 States,’ Amaechi Says ADC Will Win North-East, North-West
item.description: The vice-presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Rotimi Amaechi, has expressed confidence that the party will defeat the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the North East and North West. Speaking at a presidential rally in Bauchi State on Saturday, Amaechi said that while the ADC has the support of 13 northern states in the two regions, President Bola Tinubu of the APC has five in the South West, adding that the sixth state would vote for the Allied Peoples Movement, which has Governor Seyi Makinde as its presidential candidate. The former Rivers State governor said that the ADC would wipe out corruption, tackle insecurity, and make sure farmers can return to their farms. He also urged Nigerians to vote and protect their votes. Watch the video below. item.title: 32 Years Later, Star Trek's Most Important Movie Is Officially Free on Streaming
item.description: Released in 1994 and now streaming free on Pluto TV, Star Trek: Generations brought Captain James T. Kirk (William Shatner) and Captain Jean-Luc Picard ( Patrick Stewart ) together on the big screen for the first and only time. The result was a movie that divided fans, delivered one of the franchise's most controversial deaths, and destroyed one of television's most beloved starships. Yet more than three decades later, Generations deserves another look, particularly for what it has to say about growing older, accepting loss, and knowing when it's time to move on.

item.title: De la Fuente adamant there is no racism in Spain despite England reminder to players
item.description: England’s first game in Madrid since racist abuse in 2004 De la Fuente tells Tuchel ‘we’re not racists, none of us’ Luis de la Fuente has told Thomas Tuchel there is no racism in Spain after the England coach’s admission that he would remind his players of the anti-racism protocol prior to their meeting at the Metropolitano on Sunday night. This will be the first time the countries play each other in Madrid since some of England’s black players were subjected to racist abuse in a match at the Santiago Bernabéu in 2004 . And although England have returned to Spain three times without incident since then, twice in Seville and once in Alicante, Tuchel was asked on Friday about going back in the buildup to Sunday’s game. The England coach replied that England “will not expect anything [untoward]” but also said: “maybe we take our five minutes to inform the players about the protocol if there is a precedent [in Madrid].” Continue reading...

item.title: Obasanjo urges Nigerian youths to shun divisive, discriminatory campaigns
item.description: Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has called on Nigerian youths to shun campaign of division, segregation, discrimination and marginalisation. Obasanjo made the call on Saturday after receiving an honorary doctorate degree conferred on him by the Skyline University of Nigeria in Kano. He was conferred with the honour alongside former Executive Secretary, National Universities Commission (NUC), Prof. Abubakar Adamu-Rasheed and Mrs. Vadana Luthra. The former president, who addressed the gathering through a recorded video, said the youths, irrespective of their tribe, religion and age, must be the architects of their own future and fortune, noting they have to struggle for what they want, as salvation will not come from heaven. He said himself, and the late Head of State Murtala Muhammad spearheaded the change in the country. Obasanjo said the youths have to be positively disruptive to bring about the desired change. “Most of the leaders of the immediate, pre and post-independent era were young and active. “They went for change, and they made it happen. Nigeria, as a whole, benefited from their activism. “Let me name two – Aminu Kano and Enahoro. The military era was not much different.” Earlier, the Vice Chancellor, Prof. Ajith Kumar, announced approval of new programmes by the National Universities Commission (NUC), adding that the university was the first in North-West Nigeria to receive approval for the B.Sc. Artificial Intelligence programme. He said the development further demonstrates its commitment to advancing technology-driven education in the region. Kumar said the institution has awarded a 50% scholarship to all toppers to pursue their postgraduate programmes at the university. A total of 237 students graduated with various degrees at the institution’s 5th convocation ceremony. (NAN) The post Obasanjo urges Nigerian youths to shun divisive, discriminatory campaigns appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: [VIDEO] Atiku Promises To Resume Oil Exploration In Kolmani, Revive Mabilla Power Project
item.description: The presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, has promised to resume oil exploration activities at the Kolmani oil field, which he said were suspended under the present administration. He also pledged to restore electricity subsidies and revive work on the abandoned Mambilla Hydroelectric Power Project in the North-East. ﻿ Atiku made these promises during his presidential campaign rally in Bauchi State on Saturday. Speaking at the rally, he said, “I will restore electricity subsidies. I also promise to restore security in the North-East sub-region and the country at large. I further promise to continue oil exploration activities in Kolmani so that we can have additional sources of revenue.” On his part, Director-General of the ADC Presidential Campaign, Mr. Austin Akobundu, criticised what he described as the poor governance and misguided policy decisions of the present administration. “There is hunger in the land, and the man who will eradicate it is Atiku,” he said. In the last general election, Atiku secured a significant number of votes in Bauchi State while contesting on the platform of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). The post [VIDEO] Atiku Promises To Resume Oil Exploration In Kolmani, Revive Mabilla Power Project appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: 2027: I’m For Any Coalition That Supports Tinubu’s Re-Election — Gov Eno
item.description: Governor Umo Eno of Akwa Ibom State has thrown his weight behind the Rainbow Coalition led by Federal Capital Territory Minister Nyesom Wike, saying that he will back any coalition that supports President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in the 2027 general elections. ﻿ Eno stated this while fielding questions during a media chat on Saturday. “That Rainbow Coalition is simply saying that we support President Tinubu as the President,” he said. “If I will join and be a member of any coalition — whether it is rainbow, call it any name. Any coalition that the central point is supporting the re-election of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, I am for it.” The governor said that the relationship between the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Akwa Ibom is “good on the ground”. Eno, who is seeking re-election on the platform of the APC after his defection from the PDP in June 2025, said the two parties had agreed to support Tinubu, the Senate President, Godswill Akpabio, and himself in the 2027 general elections. “I will work with all of them, and I think we are good on the ground in Akwa Ibom when it comes to PDP-APC relationship,” the governor said. “We have agreed on the fact that we are supporting the President, we are supporting the Senate President, we are supporting the governor, and we have our clear understanding about those things.” The Rainbow Coalition is spearheaded by Wike to galvanise support for the re-election bid of President Tinubu in 2027. But the coalition has faced opposition from leaders of the APC. In October, 2026, Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma said that the Rainbow Coalition has no presence in the state. Speaking during the distribution of campaign vehicles under the PBAT Door-to-Door Movement in the state, Uzodimma insisted that the APC would secure victory in the 2027 elections through organic votes. The governor maintained that the APC was the only recognised political party in the state and urged supporters to vote for the party’s candidates across all levels in the 2027 general elections. ﻿ Similarly, Zamfara State Governor Dauda Lawal told the minister to make his political position clear over his involvement with the coalition, insisting that he cannot simultaneously support the APC and other political parties. “Our message is very, very clear: be on one side, you can’t be on two sides. If you are in APC, please come out and support the APC, not you are supporting APC here, and you are supporting some other political parties somewhere else,” he said during an interview with Channels Television’s Inside Sources on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York in October. The post 2027: I’m For Any Coalition That Supports Tinubu’s Re-Election — Gov Eno appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: FRSC confirms one dead, eight injured in Anambra multiple crash
item.description: The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC), Anambra State Sector Command, has confirmed one death and eight injuries in a multiple-vehicle crash at Agu-Awka, Immigration Junction, along the Awka-Enugu Expressway. The sector commander, Corps Commander Bridget Asekhauno, personally led the rescue efforts following the crash. Asekhauno told the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Saturday that the crash occurred at about 8.45 a.m. and involved a Sinotruck trailer, a Toyota Camry and a TVS commercial tricycle. She said that the vehicles had registration numbers AAA920YN, ENU622DR and NSH684VC, respectively. “Preliminary investigations indicated excessive speeding and inadequate construction warning signs as suspected factors responsible for the crash. “An eyewitness account indicated that the trailer, while descending a slope, noticed a diversion sign and attempted to manoeuvre into another lane. “The trailer reportedly collided sideways with the Toyota Camry, which subsequently hit the tricycle from behind, while the trailer somersaulted,” she said. The sector commander said that nine persons were involved in the crash, with one confirmed dead and eight sustained varying degrees of injuries. She added that five of the injured victims were taken to hospital for medical attention. According to her, the FRSC rescue team promptly mobilised to the scene to manage traffic and clear the obstruction. “The prompt intervention ensured the clearance and reopening of the blocked diversion route to motorists,” she said. Asekhauno expressed condolences to the family of the deceased and wished the injured victims a speedy recovery. She urged construction companies to provide adequate and visible warning signs, particularly around construction zones and diversion points, to guide motorists and prevent avoidable crashes. She also advised motorists to observe speed limits, exercise caution around diversions and construction areas as well as pay attention to road signs and traffic instructions. The sector commander reiterated FRSC’s commitment to prompt emergency response, effective traffic management and the protection of lives and property on Nigerian roads. (NAN) The post FRSC confirms one dead, eight injured in Anambra multiple crash appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time Is Actually the Perfect Way to Introduce Kids to Nintendo
item.description: Walk into The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time ’s Kokiri Forest, and it feels like you’re walking into a picture book. Especially in the remake, everything is moss-green and dappled with light. Fairies flit about. Kokiri children are rhythmically attending to their tasks. Everyone is friendly, everything is beautiful, and the world both feels safe and makes sense. Then you walk into the Great Deku Tree and spiders start falling from the ceiling. My daughter screamed. I jumped, too, and I knew they were coming.

item.title: Lookman ruled out of Tanzania return leg with knee ligament sprain
item.description: Super Eagles forward Ademola Lookman has been ruled out of Nigeria’s 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying return-leg fixture against Tanzania following a knee ligament sprain. Promise Efoghe, Super Eagles Media Officer, confirmed the development to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Saturday. “Scan has revealed Ademola Lookman suffered a sprain in his knee ligament during yesterday’s match. “This rules him out of Nigeria’s next AFCON qualifier against Tanzania in Zanzibar on Tuesday,” Efoghe said. The injury was sustained during Nigeria’s 3-1 victory over Tanzania in their Matchday Three encounter at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, Uyo, on Friday. Lookman’s absence will be a setback for the Super Eagles as they prepare for the return fixture against the Taifa Stars. The Athletico Madrid forward has been an important attacking option for Nigeria, providing creativity, pace and goal-scoring threat in the final third. NAN reports that Friday’s victory strengthened Nigeria’s position in the qualifying campaign, taking their points tally to six. The Super Eagles will now travel to Zanzibar for Tuesday’s Matchday Four encounter, hoping to consolidate their position in the group. Nigeria will be seeking another positive result against Tanzania as the race for qualification for the 2027 AFCON finals gathers momentum. Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda are already guaranteed places at the tournament as co-hosts, leaving the remaining qualification spots to be contested by other countries. The 2027 AFCON finals will be jointly hosted by the three East African countries. (NAN) The post Lookman ruled out of Tanzania return leg with knee ligament sprain appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Magic: The Gathering is getting a Netflix animated series. For real this time.
item.description: "It's really happening. I promise. For real." Those are the first words from Roy Graham, Head of Story at Magic: The Gathering , in a video posted yesterday announcing Planeswalker , the animated series heading to Netflix in 2027. An animated Magic: The Gathering series was first teased back in 2019 with Joe and Anthony Russo at the helm. But that fell apart. In 2024, Netflix announced it still planned to make a series based on the game, but it decided to rework it from the ground up. item.title: Soludo demands reopening of Anambra court of appeal
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has called for the immediate reopening of the Court of Appeal in the state, arguing that the volume of litigation generated by Anambra, which he said is second only to Lagos, justifies its continued operation. Soludo made the demand during a church service marking the commencement of the 2026/2027 Legal Year of the Anambra State Judiciary. He also urged the Nigerian legal profession to abandon imported wigs and gowns in favour of locally produced alternatives, saying the continued importation of legal attire amounts to exporting employment opportunities that could be created in Nigeria. The special service was presided over by the Bishop of Aguata, Supervising Bishop of the Diocese of Awka and Coordinating Bishop of the Province on the Niger, Rt. Rev. Samuel Ezeofor. It was attended by judicial officers, legal practitioners and government functionaries. Addressing the gathering, Soludo reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to improving justice delivery but expressed concern over the continued closure of the Court of Appeal in Anambra. “Anambra, after Lagos, generates more cases. We are more deserving to have the Court of Appeal. “The Court of Appeal in Anambra should not be closed for one day if merit and need happen to be the criteria. Come and open your court,” he said. The governor also reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to the welfare of judicial officers and the provision of necessary infrastructure for the judiciary. He noted that the state’s plea-bargaining initiative was helping to decongest correctional facilities. On the need to promote local industries, Soludo challenged lawyers and judicial officers to embrace Nigerian-made legal attire rather than continue importing wigs and gowns. “Can we change the law regalia into what is made in Nigeria? We are creating jobs abroad by importing all the regalia you wear. “Let us eat what we produce and wear what we make. That is the way to help the economy. I wear Akwete to promote Made-in-Nigeria,” he said. The governor, who is known for wearing Akwete fabric, said adopting locally produced materials would support domestic industries and create employment opportunities. On security, Soludo highlighted the cooperation among the executive, legislature and judiciary, crediting the state’s Homeland Security Law with strengthening the security architecture and restoring calm in different parts of Anambra. “We may have different branches of government, but we have one objective: the security and welfare of Ndi Anambra,” he said. Addressing the crisis within the Awka Diocese of the Anglican Communion, the governor said his administration had maintained neutrality, describing the dispute as a private affair of the Anglican Church in Anambra and Nigeria. He, however, called for an amicable resolution, stressing that the government’s responsibility was to maintain law and order. In his remarks, the Chief Judge of Anambra State,

item.title: Don’t disappoint Nigeria’s founding fathers, Jonathan warns political leaders
item.description: Former President Goodluck Jonathan has called on Nigeria’s political leaders to rebuild the country, warning against disappointing the founding fathers. This ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‌⁠​‌‍​‌‌​is contained in a statement issued by the former president’s Media Adviser, Mr Ikechukwu Eze, in Abuja on Saturday. Eze quoted Jonathan as making the call while delivering his address at a colloquium organised in honour of the 162nd birth anniversary of a nationalist, Pa Herbert Macaulay, at Nigerian Institute of International Affairs (NIIA), Lagos on Saturday. Jonathan, who was the chairman of the occasion, challenged Nigeria’s political leaders and citizens to reflect on whether the country had lived up to the dreams and aspirations of its founding nationalists. He asked whether Herbert Macaulay, Nnamdi Azikiwe, Obafemi Awolowo, Ahmadu Bello and other heroes of the independence struggle would be proud of today’s Nigeria or regret the outcome of their sacrifices. Speaking on the theme “Nationalism and Nation Building”, the former president said the vision of Nigeria’s founding nationalists went beyond the transfer of political power from colonial authorities to Nigerians. “They envisaged a sovereign, united and prosperous country where citizens would enjoy equal rights, economic opportunities, quality education, accessible healthcare and the benefits of accountable governance,” he said. Jonathan appealed that Nigeria must not allow its founding nationalists to regret the struggle they waged for independence. According to him, the greatest tribute to the nation’s heroes is not merely to celebrate their birthdays or preserve their monuments but to build a country that reflects the ideals for which they sacrificed. “We must not make Herbert Macaulay, Nnamdi Azikiwe, Obafemi Awolowo, Ahmadu Bello and the other founding nationalists regret, even in their graves, the struggle they waged for our independence,” he said. Jonathan urged the present generation to ensure that today’s national challenges were not allowed to become the inheritance of their children and grandchildren. He expressed concern that 66 years after independence, Nigeria had yet to substantially realise many of these aspirations. item.dc:creator: Ayobami
item.content:encoded: Former President Goodluck Jonathan has called on Nigeria’s political leaders to rebuild the country, warning against disappointing the founding fathers. This ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‍‌⁠​‌‍​‌‌​is contained in a statement issued by the former president’s Media Adviser, Mr Ikechukwu Eze, in Abuja on Saturday. Eze quoted Jonathan as making the call while delivering his address at a colloquium organised in honour of the 162nd birth anniversary of a nationalist, Pa Herbert Macaulay, at Nigerian Institute of International Affairs (NIIA), Lagos on Saturday. Jonathan, who was the chairman of the occasion, challenged Nigeria’s political leaders and citizens to reflect on whether the country had lived up to the dreams and aspirations of its founding nationalists. He asked whether Herbert Macaulay, Nnamdi Azikiwe, Obafemi Awolowo, Ahmadu Bello and other heroes of the independence struggle would be proud of today’s Nigeria or regret the outcome of their sacrifices. Speaking on the theme “Nationalism and Nation Building”, the former president said the vision of Nigeria’s founding nationalists went beyond the transfer of political power from colonial authorities to Nigerians. “They envisaged a sovereign, united and prosperous country where citizens would enjoy equal rights, economic opportunities, quality education, accessible healthcare and the benefits of accountable governance,” he said. Jonathan appealed that Nigeria must not allow its founding nationalists to regret the struggle they waged for independence. According to him, the greatest tribute to the nation’s heroes is not merely to celebrate their birthdays or preserve their monuments but to build a country that reflects the ideals for which they sacrificed. “We must not make Herbert Macaulay, Nnamdi Azikiwe, Obafemi Awolowo, Ahmadu Bello and the other founding nationalists regret, even in their graves, the struggle they waged for our independence,” he said. Jonathan urged the present generation to ensure that today’s national challenges were not allowed to become the inheritance of their children and grandchildren. He expressed concern that 66 years after independence, Nigeria had yet to substantially realise many of these aspirations. According to him, while Nigeria has recorded progress in several areas, patriotism demands the courage to confront its shortcomings, including leadership failures, institutional weaknesses, corruption, policy inconsistency, inadequate infrastructure, insecurity and over-dependence on raw material exports. Jonathan challenged Nigeria to learn from countries such as South Korea, India and Singapore, which had made remarkable advancement in industrialisation, technology, education, healthcare and human development. He noted that Nigeria’s enormous human and natural resources should have translated into comparable levels of development, questioning the obstacles that had continued to constrain the country’s potential. Distinguishing between independence and nation-building, Jonathan said that while winning independence was a historic achievement, building a prosperous, united and developed country remained an unfinished national responsibility. Looking ahead to Nigeria’s centenary of independence in 2060, he urged the present generation to begin asking what kind of country it intended to bequeath to future generations. He said the next 34 years must be used to establish measurable national development targets, strengthen institutions and build a productive economy capable of creating opportunities for young Nigerians. The former president also called for renewed commitment to Pan-Africanism, stressing that political independence must be complemented by economic emancipation, technological advancement, educational development and stronger continental integration. He particularly urged young Nigerians to see themselves as inheritors of the nationalist struggle, noting that the responsibility of advancing the ideals of freedom now rested on their shoulders through innovation, enterprise, civic participation and responsible citizenship. Outlining four critical areas requiring urgent attention, Jonathan called for comprehensive democratic reforms to strengthen popular participation, the rule of law, judicial independence, human rights and accountability. He also advocated reforms in political recruitment, insisting that competence, capacity and merit must take precedence over ethnic, religious and regional considerations in the selection of political leaders. On education, he called for a functional system that would prioritise technological advancement, innovation and knowledge production, adding that Nigerian universities must aspire to compete among the world’s leading institutions rather than remaining largely centres of knowledge consumption. He further emphasised the need to build strong, credible and independent institutions, stressing that sustainable national development would depend on strong institutions rather than the influence of individual leaders. Recalling the controversy surrounding Nigeria’s 2014 centenary celebrations, Jonathan said he had supported the commemoration in spite of criticisms from those who believed the country had not achieved sufficient progress to justify celebrating its 100 years of amalgamation. He explained that the importance of remembering history lies in understanding the nation’s journey, assessing its present condition and drawing lessons for a better future. The former president urged the organisers of the colloquium to move beyond historical reflections and generate concrete recommendations for repositioning Nigeria ahead of its 100th independence anniversary. ( NAN ) The post Don’t disappoint Nigeria’s founding fathers, Jonathan warns political leaders appeared first on Vanguard News .
